Brazilian police have arrested alleged serial killer Jorlan Lopes da Silva, who is accused of murdering 16 people over the past three months and is suspected of killing dozens more over the past 20 years.
Police revealed that, during the manhunt, da Silva hid in camps he built in the forest and was eventually found disguised as a woman while carrying a small child who was not related to him.
Da Silva, 33, operated in the isolated area of Mulungu in Paraiba state in northeastern Brazil, where locals nicknamed him “the mosquito” because of his thin build.
Douglas Garcia, the investigator who led the two-day operation that ended with da Silva’s capture on September 13, said his slight build had helped him evade arrest for years and hide in makeshift camps in dense vegetation.
“Jorlan lived mainly in the forests, which is why it was so difficult to locate him and connect him to crimes that initially did not appear to be related,” Garcia said.
Garcia said police were able to link da Silva to other crimes after he shot and killed an 18-year-old in a square in Mulungu. According to the investigator, the suspected serial killer claims he attacked only criminals, but evidence gathered so far suggests otherwise.
Garcia also said da Silva has provided evidence indicating that he committed additional crimes beyond those for which he is currently facing charges. According to the investigator, da Silva himself said he had killed about 80 people over the course of his life, the first when he was just 13 years old.
Garcia stressed that he could not provide further details about the additional crimes because some investigations are still underway, while others involving unsolved cases are now being reopened. The identities of the victims and details of the circumstances of their deaths are also being kept confidential to allow prosecutors to carry out their work.
Da Silva was captured wearing a black dress with white stripes, a wig and nail polish. He also was wearing sunglasses and carrying a 2-year-old child whom authorities confirmed was not a relative, though they did not provide further details.
“We caught him because he was unable to reach his tent in the forest, so out of desperation he obtained this disguise, took this baby who was not his and was eventually arrested,” Garcia said.
Police had previously said da Silva was a member of a criminal gang that murdered dozens of people in the area.
He denies any connection to local gangs and told investigators at the time of his arrest that he had been waging a “personal war.”

Which Dutch city actually fits your budget and lifestyle in 2026

Unknown Publisher
2026-09-22

Partner content
Which Dutch city actually fits your budget and lifestyle in 2026
Moving to the Netherlands means picking not just a country but also a city, and in 2026 that choice matters more than it used to. Rents in the unregulated sector rose 7.3% nationally over the past year, according to the latest Pararius Huurmonitor, pushing the average to roughly €21 per square metre. But that average hides a lot of variation. Amsterdam, Rotterdam, Utrecht, The Hague, and Eindhoven, the so-called G5, each behave quite differently right now, and the gap between them is worth understanding before you commit to a lease.
Here’s how the five compare.
Amsterdam is still the most expensive place to rent in the country by a wide margin, at €28.53 per square metre after a further 5.1% rise this year. That premium buys you the strongest job market for tech, finance, and creative roles, plus the density of international life that draws people here in the first place. An 80m² apartment typically runs €2,300 to €2,500 a month before utilities. If your work is anchored in the city, it’s worth starting your search among the apartments in Amsterdam currently listed.
Rotterdam had one of the sharpest price increases of any G5 city this year, up 10.4% to €22.78 per square metre, and it’s still noticeably cheaper than Amsterdam for comparable space. The city’s pull comes from its modern skyline, its logistics and maritime industry, and an international business culture that doesn’t feel like a smaller copy of the capital. You’ll generally get more square metres for your budget here. Current listings for apartments in Rotterdam are a reasonable place to gauge what that looks like in practice.
The Hague rose 6.5% in price this year to €22.42 per square metre and remains a common choice for people working at the international courts, embassies, or corporate headquarters based there. It has a slower pace than Rotterdam or Amsterdam, more green space, and the coastline is a short cycle away. Neighbourhoods range from the stately Statenkwartier to livelier, more central pockets, so it’s worth browsing a spread of apartments in The Hague before narrowing down an area.
Utrecht climbed 5.9% to €21.61 per square metre and sits at the literal centre of the country’s rail network, which matters more than it might sound. The city has the Netherlands’ largest university, a well-preserved medieval core, and a train commute of 30 minutes or less to nearly any other major Dutch city. That combination of culture and connectivity keeps competition for listings tight. Have a look through apartments in Utrecht to see what’s currently on the market.
Eindhoven posted the second-largest increase in the G5 this year, up 10.0% to €19.55 per square metre, still the most affordable of the five despite that jump. The city runs on ASML, Philips, and a wider “Brainport” ecosystem of tech and engineering firms, which explains why it draws a heavily specialised international workforce. If that’s your field, apartments in Eindhoven are where to start looking.
What this means for your search: In a market this tight, landlords generally expect a gross income of three to four times the monthly rent, and they’ll want to see it upfront. Have your employment contract, recent payslips, and a short summary of your rental history ready before you start applying, since properties in demand can be gone within days. Pararius only lists properties from verified, professional agents, which at least removes one layer of risk from an already competitive process. You can view all listings here.

Economic Watch: Chinese companies willing to prosper together with their global partners
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-22
20:41:13 CST
21:41:13 KST

HEFEI, Sept. 22 (Xinhua) -- At an exhibition area, a bright green SUV with a boxy shape and sturdy-looking lines attracts crowds of visitors. Inside the car, visitors marvel at the spacious interior and intelligent driving systems.
The vehicle, present at the ongoing World Manufacturing Convention in Hefei, capital of east China's Anhui Province, is the outcome of a collaboration between British automaker Jaguar Land Rover and China's Chery Automobile, with the two sides bringing together their respective strengths in vehicle design, manufacturing and intelligent technologies.
Decades ago, China's auto industry largely looked overseas for advanced vehicle models, technologies and production systems. Today, Chinese automakers are bringing their own strengths in electrification and intelligent vehicles into joint ventures and other partnerships, working with global partners to develop products for markets around the world.
"We want to build mutual advantage and look at ways in which our trade and investment can really help each other," said Peter Wilson, British ambassador to China. He said the two countries can do more research and development together, with their advanced technologies being highly complementary.
The goal, Wilson said, is to build "more of a genuine partnership" rather than simply having each side sell products to the other, adding that there is significant potential for further cooperation.
The United Kingdom is the guest country of honor in this year's convention. Along with Chinese companies, more than 40 foreign enterprises from the United States, France, Russia and other countries are exhibiting in the event.
"There are many possibilities for partnerships," said Jonathan Zeidler, personal assistant to the CEO of Kling PM GmbH, a German management company for energy, grid infrastructure and battery storage.
The company is already cooperating with Chinese partners, Zeidler said, adding that it is interesting to see Chinese companies invest in Germany, cooperate with local businesses and bring skilled employees to the country.
In the first quarter of 2026, Anhui, a manufacturing powerhouse in emerging sectors, registered 82 overseas investment projects filed by local companies, up 41.4 percent year on year and 3.2 times that of 2021, official data showed.
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian recently said at a media conference that China stands ready to work with countries around the world to continue dialogue and cooperation in frontier fields such as artificial intelligence and embodied intelligence, turning Chinese innovation and manufacturing into a genuine driving force for common development.
Cooperation potential can be unlocked through technological connectivity, joint standard-setting and market sharing, and innovation dividends can be better delivered to humanity, he added.
Li Zhen, chairman of Hefei-based leading lithium battery maker Gotion High-tech Co., Ltd., said the company has established 10 industrial bases across Europe and Africa, the Asia-Pacific region and the Americas.
"Gotion follows one principle in expanding its global footprint: to pursue localized development by establishing factories, R&D, jobs and supply chains in local markets and growing together with local partners," Li said.
Overseas business now accounts for about 30 percent of its total business, and the company plans to achieve a 1:1 ratio between overseas and domestic production capacity in the future.
"We have always believed that helping others succeed is the key to achieving our own success," Li said. ■

2026-09-22
20:41:04 CST
21:41:04 KST

TOKYO, Sept. 22 (Xinhua) -- The death toll rose to six on Tuesday, with six others still missing, after heavy rain from a large typhoon battered the Kanto region in eastern Japan and triggered landslides and flooding a day earlier, local media reported.
Among the deaths, five were confirmed in Chiba Prefecture, east of Tokyo, including a man in his 50s who died after falling into a bamboo grove while operating heavy machinery to clear mud and debris from a landslide. The others were in their 70s and 80s, according to Kyodo News.
Another death was confirmed in Yokosuka, Kanagawa Prefecture, also near Tokyo, where a woman in her 60s died on Monday after a landslide struck her home and sent mud pouring into the house.
Police and firefighters are continuing to search for the missing people.
Typhoon Dujuan, which approached Japan's eastern Pacific coast on Monday and is now moving away, brought record rainfall to the Kanto region and the Izu Islands, triggering a series of landslides and river flooding.
Rainfall in Oshima Town in the Izu Island chain over the 48 hours to 8 p.m. local time on Monday reached 832 mm, more than 2.4 times the town's average rainfall for the entire month of September and the highest since records began, according to public broadcaster NHK. A top-level landslide warning was temporarily issued for the town on Monday.
The typhoon, coming in the middle of the country's Silver Week holidays, was particularly problematic for Chiba, where intense rain inundated houses and roads and temporarily cut off electricity to about 58,000 households early Tuesday, Kyodo News said.
The typhoon also disrupted transportation, forcing All Nippon Airways and Japan Airlines to cancel more than 270 flights, mainly those to and from Tokyo's Haneda airport, affecting about 40,000 people in total. ■

Swimming roundup: China collects another Asian record, four more titles at Asian Games
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-22
20:40:59 CST
21:40:59 KST

TOKYO, Sept. 22 (Xinhua) -- China had four more gold medals in its swimming haul at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Tuesday, with Zhang Zhanshuo claiming his second title here, Peng Xuwei setting an Asian record in women's 200m backstroke and Li Bingjie successfully defending her title in women's 400m free.
China also secured the men's 4x100m medley relay victory.
Zhang, 19, stormed to victory in the men's 1,500m freestyle in 14 minutes 42.42 seconds, finishing ahead of Japan's Tabuchi Kaito in 14:45.99 and teammate Imafuku Kazushi in 14:54.37.
It was Zhang's second gold of the Games. A day earlier, he anchored China's men's 4x200m freestyle relay team to victory, producing a 1:42.92 split and overtaking Japan in the final 50 meters as China clocked an Asian record of 7:00.17.
"I just don't want to lose," Zhang said after completing what he called the toughest challenge of the Games. "I think that will give me more motivation and make me look forward to the races ahead."
Peng defended her women's 200m backstroke title in 2:05.77 to refresh the previous 16-year Asian record set in Guangzhou Games. Teammate Sun Mingxia took silver in 2:08.65, while Japan's Rio Shirai claimed bronze in 2:08.70.
"2:06.46 (the previous record) has always been a guiding light for me, encouraging me to keep improving and serving as a goal I have pursued," Peng said. "I hope this new record can inspire more Asian backstroke swimmers to challenge me and push each other forward."
China added another gold in the women's 400m freestyle, where Li Bingjie retained her Asian Games title in 4:02.71. Li said she believed there was still room for improvement.
"I think my potential lies in my ability to finish strong. When I raced against Katie Ledecky and other strong swimmers, I felt I could really tap into my potential when I had someone to chase down in the latter stage of the race," she said.
In the women's 100m freestyle, 200m free winner Siobhan Haughey of Hong Kong, China claimed her second gold in 52.45, while China's Yu Yiting secured silver in 53.21 and teammate Cheng Yujie took bronze in 53.47.
Japan grabbed the sole swimming gold in the men's 400m individual medley, as Kojima Yumeki touched first in a new Games record of 4:07.02, followed by compatriot Matsushita Tomoyuki in 4:09.64. China's Wang Shun took bronze in 4:14.59.
For Wang, a five-time Asian Games veteran, the bronze added another medal to his durable career. "Every Games have left me with many wonderful memories," Wang said, adding that he hoped more young Chinese athletes would compete on the world stage and achieve better results.
The night ended with a relay gold for China. In the men's 4x100m medley relay, China held off a late challenge from Japan to win in 3:27.89. Japan cut the gap to just 0.29 seconds with 350 meters to go, but the Chinese quartet of Xu Jiayu, Dong Zhihao, Xu Fang and Pan Zhanle held firm through the final turn to touch first. South Korea took the bronze.
Asked about the pressure as Japan closed in, backstroke veteran Xu said he never lost faith in his teammates. "Although we have young swimmers on the team, we've been working together for four years. So we trust each other," he said.
Looking ahead to his next relay on Thursday, 100m freestyle winner Pan acknowledged that it would be "a big challenge," with South Korea expected to pose a strong challenge. ■

Players of China celebrate victory after the final match of Women's Volleyball between China and Japan at the 20th Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026 in Komaki, Japan, Sept. 22, 2026. (Xinhua/Jia Haocheng)
NAGOYA, Japan, Sept. 22 (Xinhua) -- Defending champion China claimed its 10th Asian Games women's volleyball gold medal with a 3-0 victory over Japan in the final here Tuesday.
The teams traded points early in the first set. Midway through the set, China gradually pulled ahead and sealed a 25-19 win.
China maintained a narrow lead throughout the second set. Both sides ramped up their intensity, staging several long rallies before China closed out the set 25-20.

China edged Thailand 3-2 in Monday's semifinal, avenging their loss in last month's Asian Women's Volleyball Championship final and advancing to the gold-medal match against Japan. In the day's other semifinal, Japan beat South Korea 3-0.

NAGOYA, Japan, Sept. 22 (Xinhua) -- Japan's Aiko Sugihara claimed gold in the women's artistic gymnastics all-around at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Tuesday, ending China's run of 13 consecutive Asian Games titles.
In the women's qualification competition largely contested between gymnasts from China and Japan, Sugihara won the all-around title with 55.599 points, edging China's Ke Qinqin by 0.4 points. Japan's Misa Nishiyama took bronze with 55.032, while China's Zhang Qingying finished fourth.
Sugihara made a slow start, placing eighth on the uneven bars in the opening rotation. Her Japanese teammates, however, made a strong impression on the apparatus, with Nishiyama scoring 14.533 and Mana Okamura 14.066.
China's gymnasts, all making their Asian Games debuts, had mixed results on the uneven bars. Zhang and Ke finished second and third in the rotation, while Qiu Qiyuan fell from the high bar and Du Siyu made a heavy landing on her dismount.
Qiu bounced back on the balance beam, posting the highest score of 14.833, while Sugihara also recovered with 14.266 for fourth place on the apparatus.
Sugihara then delivered a strong floor exercise routine to score 13.700, the highest mark of the competition despite a 0.2-point penalty. She closed out the competition with 14.100 on the vault, the second-highest score among the gymnasts competing in the event.
Ke still had a chance to overtake Sugihara on the floor exercise, but despite earning 8.166 for execution, her difficulty score of 5.2 left her short of the Japanese gymnast. The 16-year-old Chinese gymnast eventually settled for silver.
"I didn't make any major mistakes today, which I'm happy about. My main goal was always the team event, so I'm very happy to win the individual all-around gold," Sugihara said in the post-game press conference.
"I didn't know I was in first place until after the vault, so I was quite surprised. I need to improve my floor exercise, and I'll keep my focus on tomorrow's team competition," she added.
Ke said she hoped to put the result behind her and perform closer to her training level in the upcoming team and individual events.
"This is my first Asian Games. I hope to work hard and have the chance to compete at the Asian Games again in the future, and stand on the higher step of the podium in this event," the silver medalist said.
Japan topped the women's qualification with a total score of 166.363, followed by China in second place with 165.697, marching into the women's team final. The other teams advancing to the final are the DPR Korea, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines and Chinese Taipei, with Kazakhstan named as the reserve team. ■

====================================================================================================

Global multiple sclerosis prevalence reaches 3.1 mln: study
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-22
20:40:23 CST
21:40:23 KST

MELBOURNE, Sept. 22 (Xinhua) -- About 3.1 million people worldwide are estimated to be living with multiple sclerosis (MS), a 54-percent increase over the past decade, an international study involving scientists in Australia has revealed.
The study, based on data from 133 countries and regions representing 93 percent of the world's population, provides the latest update of the Britain-based MS International Federation's Atlas of MS, the leading source of global data on the prevalence and impact of the disease, according to a statement released Tuesday by Australia's University of Tasmania (UTAS).
The findings, published in Multiple Sclerosis Journal, also reflect trends in Australia, where an estimated 37,756 people were living with MS in 2024, up 77 percent from 2010.
Professor Ingrid van der Mei, a study co-author from the Menzies Institute for Medical Research at UTAS, said the findings highlighted the growing global burden of MS and the importance of reliable data for healthcare planning and research.
The rise in prevalence did not necessarily mean MS was becoming more common, with earlier and more accurate diagnosis, improved data collection and longer life expectancy among people with MS likely contributing to the increase, researchers noted.
The findings also showed that women accounted for about 70 percent of cases globally, while more than 40,000 children and adolescents were reported to be living with MS. ■

====================================================================================================

Pentagon: laser defense needs hardware, not more demos
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-22
12:40:03 UTC
21:40:03 KST

- Assistant Secretary of War Michael Dodd said Sept. 22 that high-energy laser programs must move from demonstrations to ruggedized, fielded systems for air and missile defense.
- The U.S. Army has already committed to a Joint Laser Weapon System program and a $464.8 million laser contract with AeroVironment, while the Navy and Air Force have not.
Assistant Secretary of War for Critical Technologies Michael Dodd said the Department of War needs to move directed energy weapons out of testing and into the field, arguing in a Sept. 22 post on X that high-energy laser programs have proven the technology works and now need ruggedized, deployable systems for air and missile defense.
Dodd did not announce a new program or contract in the post. His comments add to a public campaign he has run for months, pushing the military services to commit money and timelines to fielding lasers and high-power microwave weapons rather than running further demonstrations.
The Army has already made that commitment. It awarded AeroVironment a $464.8 million contract this year for the Enduring-High Energy Laser program, a 30-kilowatt system the company has called the first production contract for a directed energy weapon in U.S. history. The Army has also agreed to transition its Joint Laser Weapon System into a formal program of record. Dodd has said his office funds prototypes and early, small-scale deployments, but expects the individual services to buy directed energy systems by the dozens or hundreds once a design proves itself.
The Navy and Air Force have not made comparable commitments. Dodd said in August he is pressing both services to follow the Army’s lead, with the Navy interested in much higher-powered systems, in the hundreds of kilowatts to a megawatt range, to defend ships against cruise missiles, a heavier requirement than the counter-drone systems the Army is pursuing.
Cost is central to the Pentagon’s argument for lasers. Officials have said a single laser shot can cost around $3.50, compared to millions of dollars for a Patriot interceptor missile, against drones that can cost tens of thousands of dollars apiece. Dodd has pointed to that mismatch as the reason directed energy needs to scale quickly, saying in March that the department aims to field directed energy weapons broadly within 36 months.
The technology still faces real constraints. Laser and microwave systems draw on rare earth elements and other critical minerals largely processed in China, and Dodd has acknowledged that per-system costs remain high because production has not scaled up. He has also pushed industry to shrink the size, weight and power demands of these weapons so they can fly on aircraft, telling contractors in August to bring “hardware we can put on a range and stress” rather than further concept presentations.
The Air Force has tested high-power microwave systems for counter-drone use, including the trailer-mounted THOR system, though its most recent publicly disclosed test dates to 2023. The Air Force Research Laboratory has said it is developing a follow-on system.

2026-09-22

Türkiye’s Treasury and Finance Minister Mehmet Simsek has said that the country’s economy remained resilient despite challenging global conditions and conflicts in the region.
He was speaking at a meeting in New York organised in cooperation with Citi as part of a three-day conference, organised by the Foreign Economic Relations Board (DEIK) and its Türkiye-US Business Council (TAIK).
The conference began on Monday and is running from September 21-23.
The opening day brought US direct investors together with Simsek, Central Bank Governor Fatih Karahan and Industry and Technology Minister Mehmet Fatih Kacir for discussions on Türkiye’s economic outlook, investment opportunities, industrial development and high technology.
“Solid foundations support our economy’s resilience against shocks,” Simsek said at the meeting, pointing to relatively high fixed capital investment, recent productivity gains, low overall indebtedness, fiscal space, reduced external vulnerabilities, rising international reserves and the continued exit from the foreign exchange-protected deposit scheme.
He said Türkiye offered investors opportunities through its large domestic market, strategic location, manufacturing and services sectors, infrastructure and skilled workforce.
Simsek also highlighted opportunities in defence, tourism, health tourism and digital services, including television series and mobile games.
He said Türkiye was accelerating its green and digital transformation, industrial transformation and productive infrastructure investments, while new tax incentives were strengthening the investment and export environment.
Karahan also provided assessments of monetary policy and the macroeconomic outlook at the meeting, while the participants discussed the government's three-year roadmap under the Medium-Term Programme announced earlier this month.
The discussions also focused on price stability, fiscal discipline, medium- and long-term growth prospects and Türkiye’s efforts to improve productivity and competitiveness.
Türkiye’s manufacturing infrastructure, transport and logistics links and access to regional markets were also highlighted, alongside investment opportunities in advanced manufacturing, defence and aerospace, healthcare, logistics, transport and digital technologies.
Türkiye seeks US cooperation in high technology
A separate roundtable organised with Concordia focused on industrial and high-technology cooperation between Türkiye and the US.
Kacir told US companies that Türkiye was building the industrial capacity, energy infrastructure, digital networks and physical connectivity needed for future technologies.
“Türkiye connects production with markets, technology with industry and Asia with Europe,” Kacir said.
“We invite American companies to produce, innovate and grow together with us in Türkiye.”
The meeting examined Türkiye’s potential to become a global hub for high-technology production and innovation, with discussions covering semiconductors, mobility, green energy, advanced manufacturing, healthcare, digital technologies, communications and space.
Participants also discussed opportunities for complementary investments across different parts of global value chains and were briefed on Türkiye’s HIT30 Investment Incentive Programme.
DEIK Chairman Nail Olpak said there were significant opportunities for joint work in industry and technology, particularly by combining Türkiye’s industrial capabilities with US strengths in artificial intelligence, semiconductors and software.
He said predictability remained one of the business community’s key expectations amid growing uncertainty in the global economy.
Murat Ozyegin, chairman of DEIK’s Türkiye-US Business Council, said maintaining the direction of Türkiye’s disinflation programme remained important despite increasingly difficult geopolitical and economic conditions.
He said attracting long-term foreign direct investment that brings technology transfer and skilled employment was among the business community’s priorities for the coming period.
Business leaders gather at New York Public Library
The conference’s first day ended with an evening reception at the historic New York Public Library, bringing together Trade Minister Omer Bolat, Kacir, Karahan, and senior representatives from the Turkish and US business communities.
The reception, organised by TAIK in cooperation with the American Turkish Business Roundtable, provided a platform for networking and discussions on investment and business opportunities between the two countries.
The conference is sponsored by Borusan Holding, Calık Holding, Fiba Holding, Kibar Holding, Koc Holding, Limak Holding, Sabancı Holding, Sahibinden, Turkish Airlines and Türk Telekom.

Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Tuesday chaired a meeting of the State-Level Vigilance and Monitoring Committee constituted for the effective implementation of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
DEHRADUN: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on tuesday chaired a meeting of the State-Level Vigilance and Monitoring Committee constituted for the effective implementation of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, and directed officials to ensure time-bound disposal of pending cases.Reviewing cases registered under the Act since 2024 where investigations are still pending, Dhami directed officials to examine the reasons for delays and take action on priority. He also called for close coordination among the police, administration and prosecution departments in long-pending and serious cases.The chief minister directed regular review of cases pending before special courts and asked officials to ensure the availability of special public prosecutors wherever required for effective prosecution.Dhami stressed that there should be no delay in disbursing prescribed relief to victims. He directed officials to separately review cases where relief payments have been delayed and said assistance to affected families should also extend, wherever required, to healthcare, education, security, rehabilitation and other eligible government schemes.The chief minister also directed officials to accord the highest priority to the safety of victims and their families in serious and sensitive cases.
He said the education of children from affected families should not be disrupted and that eligible children should be linked with scholarships and other educational assistance schemes.According to the Social Welfare Department, the state has provisions for financial assistance to victims of atrocities under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, with assistance provided at different stages depending on the nature of the offence.Dhami further directed senior-level accountability in every district for monitoring cases under the Act and called for regular training of police personnel on its provisions, investigation of sensitive cases and appropriate conduct towards victims.He also instructed the Social Welfare, Police and Prosecution departments to jointly organise refresher training programmes and directed officials to work towards developing a digital monitoring system to track investigations, court proceedings, relief payments and other assistance.Districts where progress in investigation, disposal of cases or distribution of relief is unsatisfactory should be reviewed separately, Dhami said, adding that effective practices followed by better-performing districts should be shared with others.
The chief minister also called for extensive awareness campaigns in rural and remote areas about the provisions of the Act, legal rights and assistance available to victims. He stressed that decisions taken during the meeting should not remain confined to official records and that responsibility and timelines should be fixed for every decision.The meeting was informed that 189 cases were registered under the Act in 2024 and 157 in 2025. In 2026, 116 cases had been registered up to September 15, of which 25 were under investigation.It was further informed that during 2024-25, financial assistance of Rs 228.71 lakh was provided to 205 victims; during 2025-26, Rs 143.16 lakh was provided to 127 victims; and during 2026-27, Rs 99.528 lakh had been provided to 104 victims as of September 18.Regular meetings have also been held at the state level under the chairmanship of the chief secretary and at the district level under the chairmanship of district magistrates.

El Nino strengthening rapidly, health impacts expected worldwide: UN agencies
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-22
12:37:03 UTC
21:37:03 KST

Beyza Binnur Donmez
22 September 2026•Update: 22 September 2026
El Nino is strengthening rapidly and is expected to have health impacts worldwide, with the most severe consequences likely in countries already facing weak health systems and humanitarian crises, UN agencies warned Tuesday.
"We've just lived through the two hottest months on record. Sea surface temperatures are at record levels," Armel Castellan, extreme heat adviser at the joint WHO-WMO climate and health program, told reporters in Geneva.
Castellan said El Nino is expected to peak toward the end of 2026, but stressed that its impacts would continue beyond that point.
As the event peaks, much of the Southern Hemisphere, including southern Africa, South America and Australia, will move into its hottest season in early 2027, potentially increasing risks of drought, wildfires, smoke and air pollution, he said.
Teresa Zakaria, WHO's unit head for risk reduction, humanitarian operations and climate change, told reporters that El Nino is "a significant public health threat, not just a climate phenomenon."
She said malnutrition and cholera are assessed as "very high" risks in both drought- and flood-affected settings.
More than 150 million people are already facing acute food insecurity globally, with that figure expected to increase as climate shocks disrupt food production and livelihoods, she said.
Warmer temperatures and changing rainfall could also increase transmission of mosquito-borne diseases including malaria, dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever and Zika, potentially spreading them into areas where they have not traditionally occurred.
"We have a window of opportunity to act now before these risks become crises," Zakaria said.

After floods, Nepal minister demands 'climate justice'
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-22
12:37:00 UTC
21:37:00 KST

After floods, Nepal minister demands 'climate justice'
September 22, 2026
Nepal is seeking $20 million (just under €17.5 million) from the international Loss and Damage Fund, the UN-backed mechanism designed to support countries suffering irreversible climate-related losses, Environment Minister Geeta Chaudhary said in an exclusive DW interview.
The move comes after floods and landslides killed more than 1,400 people in August and left thousands missing.
"We have already issued the official letter for the fund for the loss and damage," Chaudhary told DW. "Most of the countries have sent us a positive response."
The flash flooding caused widespread destruction across large swathes of Nepal, damaging homes, agricultural land and infrastructure. Rescue and recovery efforts are still ongoing in several areas, while authorities continue to assess the full scale of the losses.
In the Himalayan nation, the tragedy has become a powerful symbol of what developing countries describe as the unfair climate burden of contributing little to global emissions while facing disproportionate consequences.
'Sympathy alone will not work for us'
Talking to DW, Chaudhary repeatedly framed Nepal's response through the lens of climate justice, a concept that has become increasingly prominent in global climate negotiations.
"Sympathy alone will not work for us," she said. "We don't need sympathy. We need justice. It's high time. If you're not able to give us justice, then we also don't need the words."
"Those countries who are emitting the most and are able to contribute the funds, they need to pay for the climatic disasters like what we are facing," she said.
Nepal contributes roughly 0.1% of global greenhouse gas emissions. Its geography, however, makes it extremely vulnerable to climate-related risks. Rising temperatures in the Himalayas have accelerated glacial retreat and increased concerns about glacial lake outburst floods, landslides and extreme weather events across the region.
In the wake of the most recent disaster, the government has intensified calls for more adaptation financing, direct access to climate funds and stronger international commitments to fight consequences of climate change.
'The world is watching'
Chaudhary pointed to melting glaciers, warming temperatures and changes in mountain environments as factors behind the deadly floods.
"Our evidence is showing that this catastrophic event is because of climate change," Chaudhary said.
While many scientists agree that climate change increases the likelihood and severity of such events, establishing a causal relationship between a specific disaster and global warming typically requires detailed attribution studies.
Researchers are more likely to point to a combination of factors, including glacier and permafrost degradation, extreme weather conditions and geological vulnerabilities.
The Nepali government, however, insists that the connection is clear.
"We are the real example and the world is watching us," Chaudhary told DW.
Building support ahead of COP31
The minister's comments come as Nepal seeks to build momentum for COP31, the UN's annual climate conference set to be held in Turkey this November.
When asked about her government's plans for the conference, Chaudhary said "Nepal will no longer negotiate on vague promises or slow-moving traditional and development aid."
According to the minister, Nepal intends to push for greater recognition of the specific challenges facing mountainous countries, arguing that global climate discussions often overlook the risks confronting Himalayan regions.
"Mountain issues need to be addressed," she said. "The world needs to see us, that we are victimized countries. We are paying the price."
Chaudhary also pointed out that Nepal received strong backing from fellow vulnerable nations at the recent gathering of Least Developed Countries (LDCs) in Timor-Leste.
"All the LDCs stood with us," she said. "They are very concerned."
The government plans to bring climate concerns to the UN General Assembly, highlighting the recent disaster and calling for concrete support from the international community.
Nepal to improve its early warning systems
The scale of the disaster has also prompted scrutiny inside Nepal, particularly of the country's warning systems and its disaster response.
Residents in some affected areas have complained that warnings came too late or did not adequately reflect the scale of the danger.
Chaudhary defended the government's response but conceded that existing systems were overwhelmed by the sheer scale of the event.
"We had sent them messages and information," she said. "But the situation was beyond imagination."
She acknowledged that Nepal's early warning systems must improve and said authorities are now reviewing and strengthening existing monitoring mechanisms.
"Our hydrology and meteorology departments are working on that," she said.
The floods also highlighted the importance of cooperation between Nepal and its neighbors, particularly China, in monitoring river systems and glacial hazards that cut through national borders.
"We are working closely," Chaudhary said, adding that technical teams from both countries are sharing information and examining future risks.
Himalayan catastrophe as a warning for the world
For Chaudhary, the disaster is not only a national tragedy but a warning about the future.
"Our snow is melting, our lakes are in danger," the minister said.
She warned that, unless global warming is limited in line with the Paris climate agreement of 2015, vulnerable countries could face increasingly severe disasters.
Asked whether the world is acting fast enough, the minister responded: "I don't think so."

Ethiopian armed groups seek to oust government
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-22
12:36:28 UTC
21:36:28 KST

Ethiopian armed groups seek to oust government
Seven Ethiopian armed groups, including former battlefield enemies, have formed an alliance seeking to overthrow Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s government and establish a transitional administration.
The Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Alliance for Survival, unveiled on Sunday, includes the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), the Amhara Fano National Movement, and the Oromo Liberation Army, alongside four smaller groups.
In a joint statement, the groups accused Abiy’s ruling Prosperity Party of imposing “dictatorial” rule and pushing the East African country toward disintegration. “We, the peoples’ forces concerned with the survival of Ethiopia’s peoples, bear the historic responsibility of overthrowing this regime,” they declared. They pledged an inclusive transitional government tasked with ending “all wars” and organizing a national and constitutional dialogue.
The alliance urged government troops and their commanders “to join and become partners in the struggle to save” the country.” It also appealed for support from civic organizations and the international community.
Abiy’s spokesperson, Billene Seyoum, told Reuters on Monday that the groups had long collaborated with financial backing from neighboring Eritrea. Asmara has repeatedly denied allegations of supporting the groups.
The Ethiopian government says its national dialogue aims to address political divisions and internal conflicts.
Ethiopia has struggled to secure lasting stability since a November 2022 peace accord ended the two-year Tigray war, which killed hundreds of thousands. Fano fought alongside federal troops against Tigrayan forces before turning against the government in 2023. The Oromo Liberation Army has fought federal forces since 2018. Renewed clashes and reported drone strikes in Tigray have further undermined the peace accord.
The alliance members pledged to resolve their differences “peacefully.” Amhara and Tigrayan groups have competing claims to Western Tigray, which became part of Tigray when regional boundaries were redrawn in the early 1990s. Amhara nationalists dispute that allocation, and their forces took control of the area during the Tigray war.
The UN said on Monday it is “deeply concerned” by Ethiopia’s worsening security situation, including the formation of the new armed coalition and reports of continued insecurity and drone strikes. UN spokesman Stephane Dujarric urged all sides to avoid actions or rhetoric that could further escalate tensions and recommit to dialogue, saying “military action will not resolve political differences or address underlying grievances.”

MOSCOW, September 22. /TASS/. The US decision to deny Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Alexander Alimov a visa to participate in the UN General Assembly, Vladimir Zelensky’s contradictory statements and the situation in the Black Sea topped the agenda of Russian Presidential Spokesman Dmitry Peskov’s briefing on Tuesday.
TASS has compiled key statements by the Kremlin spokesman.
On US refusal to grant visa to senior Russian diplomat
- The US refusal to grant a visa to Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Alexander Alimov to participate in the UN General Assembly will be discussed during contacts between Moscow and Washington: "This will undoubtedly be on the agenda for our contacts with the Americans."
- This situation serves as another example of unfriendly actions toward Russia: "This is yet another unfriendly move toward our country."

On Zelensky’s statements
- Vladimir Zelensky’s statements are becoming increasingly contradictory with each day: "His statements on whether to stop or continue the war become increasingly contradictory with each coming day."
- Zelensky’s latest statements about a ceasefire came amid the deteriorating situation on the battlefield and economically for Ukraine: "As for such statements by Zelensky, the situation in Ukraine is clearly deteriorating day by day, both economically and on the front lines. And this trend will persist."
On Ukrainian settlement
- Russian President Vladimir Putin has always said that, regarding the Ukraine conflict, Moscow advocates for a lasting peace rather than a ceasefire, which would essentially achieve nothing: "President Putin and the Russian side have always said that we stand for a lasting peace – a peace that endures – rather than a ceasefire, which would essentially achieve nothing."

On EU sanctions
- Russia considers Western sanctions illegal and believes that they must be lifted for all Russian citizens: "We consider these sanctions illegal. We believe that these sanctions must be lifted on Usmanov, Fridman, and all Russian businessmen – just as they should be on all Russian citizens."
On situation in Black Sea

- Russia is ensuring grain supplies to foreign markets via alternative routes amid the current situation in the Black Sea: "As for Russian grain, alternative transport routes and destinations are being secured under the president’s instructions."
On UN Security Council
- Russia believes that the UN Security Council should be reformed and enlarged: "We believe that the UN Security Council should definitely be reformed. Permanent membership has to be expanded, as many states and interstate formations have emerged that should certainly have their say in the Security Council."

On Arctic
- Moscow and Washington are not discussing cooperation in the Arctic during their working contacts: "The issue of cooperation in the Arctic is not on the agenda right now."
- Western countries decline to cooperate with Moscow in the Arctic, but it does not diminish Russia’s role in the region: "The Americans and other Arctic states refuse to engage with Russia. This in no way diminishes our country’s role in Arctic affairs."

Nazi imagery nothing new for crypto casino behind Orlando fight with swastika flags, Hitler salutes

Nazi salutes. A swastika flag. Fights in the stands. They were all part of the scene at a recent combat sports event in Orlando that pitted an Israeli Jew against an avowed racist with SS bolts tattooed on his chest – and ended with the latter mocking his defeated foe as “a short little f***king Jew prick.”
The condemnation that followed the Aug. 29 event was aimed in a number of directions: at Paul Miller, the fighter who performed the Hitler salute after his win; at the attendees who returned the salute and displayed the Nazi flag; and at the Kia Center, the city-owned arena best known as the home of the NBA’s Orlando Magic, which hosted the fight night.
Politicians were shocked by the display and wrote statements condemning the event — but the Nazi symbols were nothing new for Duel, the online cryptocurrency casino behind the promotion.
Founded last year and billing itself as “the first casino that gives a f***,” Duel has used Nazi symbols and racist language in its gambling programming. And its owner, Ossi Ketola, a Finnish high-stakes poker player, is himself a self-described First Amendment absolutist with his own history of racially charged comments. He celebrated his devotion to free speech just one week after the Orlando event, in a social media post featuring a photo of himself with Donald Trump Jr.
One of Duel’s blackjack dealers, Nelli Levonyan, has worn a Nazi outfit with a swastika armband on multiple occasions while dealing cards on the blackjack stream. In a skit from the blackjack table that circulated online, a man, dressed up as an Orthodox Jew and holding an Israeli flag, attacked Levonyan by throwing coins at her. Levonyan’s character then sprayed something at the Jewish man — “Gassing!” he yelled — and said, “Go away from me, you dirty k***.”
In another blackjack stream, the dealer imitated one of the two San Diego mosque shooters, who killed five people in May. Levonyan has sung the lyrics to “Heil Hitler,” the Ye (formerly Kanye West) song, during a stream. She has also appeared alongside Miller while hosting the card game.
Earlier this month, Ketola joined a neo-fascist rally in Helsinki staged by the far-right party Sinimusta Liike, or the Blue-and-Black Movement. Ketola, who was dressed in a SpongeBob costume, livestreamed the rally and posted the footage with the title “Saving white Finland.” Speaking about immigrants, he said that people “need to be educated about how the genes work, and how these people realistically cannot be integrated here.”
Ketola heard off-camera yelling Nazi phrase 'sieg heil'
He then attended an anti-fascist rally held elsewhere in Helsinki simultaneously, prompting left-wing demonstrators to chase him and his video crew back to their car. Ketola could be heard off-camera yelling “Sieg heil” as they drove away.
“What f–king violent pussies. Imagine what f***ing leftists,” Ketola said after taking off the SpongeBob costume. “You see? These right-wing people, white people, the most friendly people. I just walked there, we didn’t say anything, we didn’t do anything — we go to these leftists, and they try to f***ing attack us. F***ing dumb stupid f***ing n***ers.”
The following night, Ketola attended the dinner with Trump and about a dozen others in Tallinn, Estonia, hosted by Studioworks, a company that develops software for online casino sites. Neither the Trump Organization, Miller, Ketola, nor Levonyan responded to requests for comment.
Duel was founded last summer and has featured prominent personalities on its streams, including boxing great Mike Tyson — who told Levonyan, “You dumb b***h, you like Hitler” — and the “looksmaxxing” influencer Braden Peters, known as Clavicular.
The fight night that it organized and promoted in Orlando was its first foray into combat sports and made for the company’s biggest splash yet. It also caught the attention of at least one watchdog and a local lawmaker.
“Right after the event there was a lot of criticism put on the venue, which didn’t have much responsibility in this, and not enough eyes on the people who actually made it happen,” Mark Pitcavage, senior fellow at the Anti-Defamation League’s Center on Extremism, told the Jewish Telegraphic Agency.
State Rep. Anna Eskamani called for the Florida Athletic Commission to revoke Duel Arena’s license. Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis appointed the commission's members, who have not commented on the event. The governor’s office did not respond to multiple requests for comment from JTA.

Pitcavage said that combat sports are “a draw for far-right extremists and white supremacists” who often view themselves as “white warriors.” He noted, however, that they make up a small portion of the participants and fans.
“It’s not at all surprising that some of them will get into various types of what they would consider manly, or warrior-like athletics,” he said.
Duel’s involvement in the Orlando event put the intersection of online gambling sites and far-right ideologies on his radar. “It’s something we’re starting to look into,” Pitcavage said. He noted that Duel is registered and licensed offshore on the autonomous island of Anjouan, making it more difficult to investigate.
Eskamani, who is running for mayor of Orlando, told JTA that Duel should not be allowed to operate in Florida, citing reasons that she says would beat the city’s First Amendment defense.
“These offshore cryptocurrency — I mean, there are so many red flags in how this entity is operating that from a purely financial security position for a public venue, I would not want to accept a reservation,” Eskamani said.

Miller known for use of racial slurs, denigration of minority groups
Miller, who has made numerous appearances on Duel’s casino games streams, has been known to use racial slurs and denigrate minority groups in his online content. Randy Fine, the Jewish Republican firebrand whose district includes Palm Coast and Daytona Beach, posted a video of the Nazi flag being unfurled and wrote, “This is not a joke, and it is not edgy. The guy who did this is old enough to know exactly what that symbol means and to know that it’s not funny. We will make an example out of him.”
Asked what he meant by making an example of the attendee, Fine told JTA, “We put the video out so he would be recognized and be held publicly accountable. Most folks are unwilling to associate with Nazis.”
Cheering Miller on ringside was Jake Shields, a former mixed martial artist-turned far-right influencer who has espoused conspiracy theories about Jews and Israel. Shields wore a shirt reading “FCK ISRL.” Myron Gaines, a prominent streamer who has spread similar conspiracy theories and performed Nazi salutes, was in the stands and told Miller before the fight, “You fight for the goyim,” according to clips shared on social media.
Pitcavage said he has been tracking a trend of the far-right getting involved in combat sports since the late 1990s, as mixed martial arts and the UFC became more mainstream and amateur gyms became widespread and increasingly accessible.
The ADL has flagged that in recent years “active clubs,” or “localized white supremacist crews” that gather for fight training, have become more common. The ADL writes that these groups “see themselves as fighters training for an ongoing war against a system that they claim is deliberately plotting against the white race.”
As news outlets covered backlash to the Orlando fight night, Duel issued its own statement saying it was horrified “to learn that a group of viewers was displaying symbols of hate at our event.” The company criticized the city’s “shocking remarks that the ‘First Amendment’ applies and that ‘free speech’ is permitted at their arena,” and pledged to “work with local activist groups to push back on this and ensure that this kind of hate does not fester ever again.”
The statement appeared to be an example of Duel trolling with deadpan, buttoned-up language. Before the fight, Ketola released a similar promotional video that appeared to condemn Miller’s views. “Paul Miller is a Nazi. Being a Nazi is bad,” Ketola narrated, over footage of him shaking his head. “We cannot support this. The only reason we are allowing him to fight is to ensure the good guys get to add another victory to their record.”
Then, after Miller’s win, Duel’s Instagram account left a comment that told a different story.
“The good guys won,” Duel wrote.

BRICS 2026 Reveals Ambition, Contradictions, and Uncertain Futures
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-22
12:33:00 UTC
21:33:00 KST

Much fanfare accompanied the two-day (September 12-13) 2026 BRICS Summit in New Delhi. The Indian government shut down the capital through road closures, dignitaries made grand statements – including, notably, one by Russian President Vladimir Putin that the “old leaders” (the G7) are being replaced by “new engines of economic growth” (BRICS countries).
The grouping of an expanded 11 full members (Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, and the United Arab Emirates) issued a 140-point declaration on topics from Bretton Woods to conflict in the Middle East. Indian Member of Parliament Vikramjit Singh Sahney proclaimed that the summit was “historic” and “a major diplomatic achievement for India under Prime Minister Narendra Modi.”
But what did the meeting actually accomplish, and what is the future of BRICS?
The BRICS New Delhi declaration made many pledges. Two of these reaffirmed the “BRICS spirit of mutual respect and understanding, sovereign equality, solidarity, democracy, openness, inclusiveness, collaboration and consensus” as well as a commitment to upholding international law. Though these sounded agreeable, “mutual respect,” “democracy,” “openness,” and “upholding international law” ring particularly hollow in view of ongoing conflicts involving some BRICS members as well as the global tilt toward autocracy in recent years.
Nevertheless, the declaration went on to stress the importance of developing nations’ promoting dialogue for a more just and stable international order. It referenced the BRICS Payment Task Force and the exploration of efficient cross-border payment mechanisms.
That said, BRICS opposes carbon border adjustment mechanisms, deeming them discriminatory toward developing nations. Though this might be true, these nations should account for the carbon output of companies in the Global South via the implementation of their own border adjustment mechanisms, which would capture not only carbon, but also tax revenue.
On the environment, the declaration acknowledged the challenges of urban development, water availability, biodiversity, desertification, deforestation and waste management. This document named a variety of new initiatives to address these problems such as the BRICS Guidelines for Disaster Management Early Warning Data Integration and the Network of BRICS Institutions to Advance Knowledge Sharing, Research and Innovation in Sustainable Lifestyles.
In terms of human rights, it affirmed the importance of intellectual property protection and economic advancement for women. But without proper execution, these statements are just words on paper.
In addition, geopolitical fault lines are hard to ignore. Brazilian economist Paulo Nogueira Batista Jr referred to India as an “outlier,” due to its ties with Israel and the United States (Batista said explicitly that he would not go as far as others in calling India a “Trojan horse” in BRICS, however).
The United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia are currently involved in direct and indirect fighting with Iran, China and India disagree over their shared border, Pakistan and trade, and Egypt and Ethiopia have unresolved issues pertaining to water rights. These are just a few of the geopolitical issues that threaten to dismantle this grouping BRIC by BRIC.
Senior Fellow at the Pune International Centre Ajit Ranade argued convincingly that the greatest achievement of the latest BRICS conference was on the sidelines in the form of bilateral engagement between India and China. With this event being the first time in seven years that Chinese President Xi Jinping has visited India, it enabled leaders of the two countries to make progress within certain compartments of their complex relationship. Any positive developments between China and India – even at the level of increased cultural exchanges and direct flights – benefits humanity.
The idea of advancing humanity by prioritizing the needs of the Global South certainly did not originate from BRICS 2026. The New Delhi Declaration made explicit reference to the 1955 Bandung Conference, where African and Asian countries expressed their commitment to the Ten Principles of Peaceful Coexistence.
Bandung signified an important step in the trajectory of countries then emerging from colonial rule, and BRICS has built upon the idealism enumerated there.
But if BRICS is to succeed, the arrangement needs to have clear membership criteria, take advantage of opportunities made available by the missteps of G7 countries (especially by the United States on climate), build robust, long-lasting supply chains within BRICS, offer attractive investment and trade deals to middle powers, and remain committed to what it favors, rather than merely what it opposes.
As Dean of International Studies at Aligarh Muslim University Aftab Alam observed, although the New Delhi Declaration described the shortcomings of the existing order, BRICS has yet to articulate clearly what a more just and equitable system would look like.
Strict World Trade Organization compliance, additional BRICS members as permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, and a strong BRICS New Development Bank – emblematic of a parallel financial system that gives developing nations more options – might define this new international order.

The Belgian Air Force has received a new batch of three F-35A Lightning II multi-role fighter jets, which arrived at Florennes Air Base after a flight from the United States.
The Belgian Air Force reported this.
The three Belgian fighter jets departed from the United States on September 15, along with three F-35As destined for the Finnish Air Force. The flight to Europe routed via the Azores with support from refueling aircraft.
Another Belgian F-35A is expected to arrive by the end of 2026. After that, the 2nd Tactical Wing at Florenne Air Base will have eight of this type of aircraft. Belgium has ordered a total of 34 F-35A fighter jets to replace its fleet of F-16s.
The arrival of new F-35As in the Belgian Air Force will determine the pace at which Belgium transfers F-16s to Ukraine. By the end of 2026, the country plans to transfer seven F-16s to Ukraine: three for combat use and four as a source of spare parts. In total, Belgium plans to transfer all 53 of its F-16s to Ukraine by the end of 2029.
Deliveries of the F-35A directly to Belgium began in 2025. Florennes has become the main base for the new fighter jets, and the aircraft are also planned to be stationed at Kleine-Brogel Air Base in the future.
At the same time, Belgium plans to expand its future F-35A fleet. Militarnyi previously reported that the country’s government is considering purchasing an additional batch of fighters as part of the Air Force’s ongoing rearmament.

U.S. Army evaluates SkyRunner flying buggy
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-22
12:32:31 UTC
21:32:31 KST

- The U.S. Army's XVIII Airborne Corps tested the SkyRunner dual-mode flying buggy during Scarlet Dragon 26-3 at Fort Bragg, North Carolina, on Sept. 16.
- The vehicle can fly up to 10,000 feet with a 120-mile range and drives up to 240 miles on the ground, and it retails for $140,000 to $150,000.
The U.S. Army’s XVIII Airborne Corps evaluated a dual-mode flying buggy called the SkyRunner during Scarlet Dragon 26-3, an experimentation exercise held at Fort Bragg, North Carolina, on Sept. 16. Soldiers tested the vehicle’s ability to shift between driving and flying in austere conditions at Holland Drop Zone.
The SkyRunner pairs an off-road buggy chassis with a ram-air parachute wing, letting it drive on rough terrain and then take off without a runway. It needs about 450 feet (137 meters) of open ground to get airborne. In the air, the vehicle can climb to a maximum altitude of 10,000 feet (3,048 meters) at a rate of 465 feet (142 meters) per minute, with a flight range of roughly 120 miles (193 km). On the ground, it can travel up to 240 miles (386 km) on a tank of fuel.
SkyRunner says a new pilot needs about 14 hours of flight instruction before flying the vehicle solo. Once airborne, the controls are simple: a left and right toggle for steering and a throttle pedal for climbing or descending. The buggy uses two separate engines, a Polaris unit for ground driving and a Rotax aircraft engine to turn the rear-mounted propeller in flight.
The company’s current retail price for the SkyRunner runs between $140,000 and $150,000. SkyRunner has pitched the vehicle to U.S. military and government buyers for over a decade, citing potential uses in reconnaissance, resupply, and casualty evacuation in places without roads or landing strips.
Scarlet Dragon 26-3 tested a range of unmanned and manned-adjacent systems alongside the SkyRunner, including a drone mothership built by Modalic and swarms of small unmanned aircraft launched from a single site. The exercise, run by the XVIII Airborne Corps at Fort Bragg, pairs soldiers with industry partners to test emerging technology under field conditions. This was the third iteration of Scarlet Dragon in the current exercise cycle, following events in December 2025 and earlier this year.
The Army has not disclosed whether it plans to buy the SkyRunner or set a timeline for further testing. The Corps has said it will continue evaluating technologies from Scarlet Dragon 26-3 during Scarlet Dragon 27-1 in April 2027, ahead of a larger exercise called Summit Strike at Fort Drum, New York, in September 2027.

Novo CEO Mike Doustdar told CNBC that the pharmaceutical giant is considering M&A opportunities as it faces growing competition in the crowded weight-loss market.
"Let's see where the gaps are, and let's go out and see who has produced or is about to introduce better drugs than we are able to do on our own, and when that gap can be filled with M&A, we are actually quite interested about it," Doustdar said on CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" on Tuesday.
He was speaking after the company faced investor pressure at its Capital Markets Day event on Monday, where it unveiled a turnaround plan that failed to convince markets it was ready to compete when the active ingredient in its weight-loss medication Wegovy starts losing key exclusivity in the early 2030s.
Novo was last seen trading just below the flatline, down 0.75%, after falling nearly 8% on Monday, its worst trading day since February.
"I think yesterday we laid out a more clear strategy of the direction we want to take the company at. We talked about diversification of the company, but yet the reaction tells me that there's still some work to do in convincing some of the investors," Doustdar said.
The company outlined plans to release over five "multi-blockbuster" drugs by 2030, which it expects to generate more than 150 billion Danish kroner ($23 billion) in sales by 2035. It also guided for revenue growth that is in line with industry peers such as Eli Lilly, AstraZeneca, Amgen, Biogen, Merck, AbbVie, and Novartis.
The plans disappointed investors who were hoping for a "miracle," especially as its target growth is in line with its peers, signalling slower progress than expected, analysts told CNBC on Monday.
Novo's key U.S. rival Eli Lilly has captured a large share of the weight loss market with its injectable GLP-1 drugs Mounjaro and Zepbound despite launching years after.
Lilly's CEO David Ricks told CNBC on Monday that a third of new GLP-1 patients are now taking its oral weight loss pill, Foundayo. "We're confident long term," he said.
While Novo's shares have declined 34% over the past year, Lilly is up just over 54% in the past 12 months.
Doustdar said the company plans to diversify beyond its core areas of diabetes and obesity, including building out its portfolio within blood and endocrine disorders, liver disease and cardiovascular disease.
"It is the right time now that I feel comfortable about the core to speak about the diversification of the company in adjacent areas that are not new to us either," he added.
"So it would be more obvious for me to imagine that we will be making more deals in areas outside of the core than in the core."
CNBC's Elsa Ohlen contributed to this report.

Macron urges von der Leyen to relax EU fuel rules as energy crunch bites

Macron urges von der Leyen to relax EU fuel rules as energy crunch bites
French President Emmanuel Macron has urged the European Commission to temporarily lower EU quality requirements for diesel and kerosene as record prices and growing fuel shortages hit France, broadcaster BFM TV has reported.
Looser standards could allow some refineries to produce 5% to 20% more, but the trade-off could mean dirtier fuel.
Macron’s push comes as the US-Israeli war on Iran disrupts flows through the Strait of Hormuz, squeezing energy markets already reshaped by the EU’s self-imposed sharp reduction in Russian imports after the 2022 escalation of the Ukraine conflict.
In a letter to European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen last week, Macron called for the temporary lowering of fuel-quality standards covering density, vaporization, and sulfur content, the outlet wrote on Monday. He said the move could deliver “significant production gains” of between 5% and 20% depending on the refinery.
Macron noted that US road diesel can contain up to 15 parts per million (ppm) of sulfur, compared with the EU limit of 10 ppm. Allowing higher sulfur levels would let refineries quickly increase fuel production as the EU grapples with shortages and soaring prices, but at the cost of higher pollution.
The French president also wants more B7 diesel, which contains up to 7% biodiesel, replaced with B10 containing up to 10%. He argued the measures would “strengthen our import and production capacities in the short term” and increase fuel available on the European market.
Paris is seeking the changes as France faces surging prices and supply strains. Fuel distributors have reported growing difficulties securing deliveries for the coming weeks, according to Macron’s letter. Europe is particularly dependent on the Middle East for refined fuels, which account for 36% of its kerosene imports and 18% of diesel imports.
Diesel prices in France hit a record €2.39 ($2.75) per liter last week, while 16% of filling stations were short of at least one type of fuel on Monday, according to government data. France consumes around 600,000 barrels of diesel a day and imports roughly half of it, Macron said.
Fuel prices have also hit record highs across the EU, with diesel averaging €2.16 per liter and gasoline €2.06 this month.
Brussels, however, is pressing ahead with plans to eliminate the remaining Russian supplies by late 2027 even as the EU scrambles for more fuel amid the Middle East crisis. Russia’s share of EU gas imports has plunged from 45% before the Ukraine conflict to 12% in 2025, while its crude share fell from 27% to around 2%.
With Russian energy supplies still being phased out, Paris is now asking Brussels to relax its own rules to get more fuel onto the market.
Global oil prices have surged above $100 per barrel as the US-Israeli war on Iran and Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure fuel fears of further supply disruptions. Brent crude recently crossed the threshold for the first time in nearly two months.

The Battle for Taiwan’s East: Taipei’s Western Pacific Strategy
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-22
12:29:00 UTC
21:29:00 KST

Since July, China has begun conducting more regularized coast guard patrols in waters east of Taiwan. These operations are, of course, partly connected to recent maritime developments involving Japan and the Philippines. Yet a broader trend is also becoming increasingly visible: the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) has stepped up both the scale and intensity of its activities in the airspace and waters east of Taiwan.
In addition to continuing its joint combat readiness patrols across the Taiwan Strait median line and into Taiwan’s southwestern airspace, the PLA has noticeably increased reconnaissance and surveillance operations to Taiwan’s east and southeast. On September 5, the PLA deployed J-11 fighters, Su-30s, H-6 bombers, Y-8 electronic warfare aircraft, KJ-500 airborne early warning and control aircraft, and other platforms, with some entering Taiwan’s southeastern airspace. During another joint combat readiness patrol on September 9, PLA aircraft operated in Taiwan’s northern, central, and eastern airspace, further demonstrating that Chinese military activity is no longer concentrated primarily west of the island.
According to data released by Taiwan’s Ministry of National Defense, PLA aircraft repeatedly operated east of Taiwan in September, including on September 5-6, September 9-10, September 14-16, and September 18-19. During the September 9 patrol, the PLA also deployed combat aircraft, support aircraft, and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), with activities extending into Taiwan’s eastern airspace.
Compared with manned aircraft, UAVs offer longer endurance, lower operating costs, and greater suitability for sustained intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance missions. The PLA’s growing use of drones east of Taiwan therefore serves not only as a form of military pressure, but also as a means of systematically collecting battlefield intelligence on Taiwan’s force posture.
Potential targets of such surveillance include air base activities in Hualien and Taitung, aircraft takeoffs, landings, and dispersal patterns, the operation of radar and air defense systems, movements of naval and air forces, and possible external reinforcement routes through waters and airspace east of Taiwan.
Cutting Taiwan’s Sea Lines of Communication
For Taiwan, the strategic importance of its eastern coastline becomes particularly apparent in a wartime scenario. In the event of a PLA attack, airports and ports along Taiwan’s western coast could be subjected to sustained strikes or interdiction by long-range rocket artillery and Dong Feng-series ballistic missiles. Eastern ports would therefore become critical rear-area logistics hubs and potential lifelines for sustaining Taiwan’s war effort.
This concept was reflected in Taiwan’s Han Kuang 42 live-fire exercise earlier this year. On August 13, Taiwan’s navy and coast guard jointly conducted blockade-breaking escort and strategic logistics transfer drills. A combined naval and coast guard formation escorted the ROCS Yushan, which was acting as a simulated merchant vessel, into Hualien Port. Civilian vehicle convoys were then used to transfer supplies inland. The exercise was intended to test Taiwan’s ability to break a maritime blockade and maintain strategic supply lines during wartime.
This is precisely the kind of contingency the PLA is likely seeking to counter.
Since July, China has used maritime law enforcement vessels to increase its presence in waters east of Taiwan. Even before that, PLA Navy warships had regularly conducted patrols and surveillance in the area. In the past, however, such activity was often reactive, particularly when Chinese vessels encountered Taiwanese surveillance ships operating in waters east of the island. Since June, Beijing appears to have increased the intensity of such patrols and begun integrating UAVs more systematically into operations east of Taiwan.
Expanding Intelligence Collection and Close-In Reconnaissance
The deeper significance of the PLA’s expanding presence east of Taiwan lies in its ability to build a more comprehensive intelligence picture of Taiwan’s eastern military infrastructure.
Under Taiwan’s longstanding defense planning, the eastern side of the island could become a critical sanctuary in wartime. Air bases, naval facilities, and other military infrastructure in eastern Taiwan may be used to disperse aircraft and warships, conduct repairs and resupply, regenerate combat power, and support possible external intervention by the United States, Japan, or other partners.
Unmanned systems can do more than conduct reconnaissance or launch direct strikes. They can also provide targeting data for long-range precision weapons, including Dong Feng-series missiles, helping the PLA build a more integrated sensor-to-shooter architecture. This reflects the PLA’s broader emphasis on integrating reconnaissance and strike capabilities into a single operational system.
If the PLA can systematically monitor patterns of military activity during peacetime — including radar activation cycles, force movements, dispersal routes, and the operating rhythms of key bases — it can improve the effectiveness of wartime joint strikes and blockade operations by the PLA Rocket Force, Air Force, and Navy.
Future indicators should therefore include the duration of PLA UAV operations east of Taiwan, the frequency of appearances by Chinese electronic intelligence and reconnaissance aircraft, and the degree of coordination between PLA aircraft and naval vessels operating east of the island.
This trend has become particularly important as Taiwan itself expands military activity in the Western Pacific. Recent developments include testing of the MQ-9B unmanned aerial system, military deployments to Orchid Island during the Han Kuang exercise, and tri-service precision munitions drills conducted in the waters east of Taiwan, including the sinking exercise involving the decommissioned frigate ROCS Lan Yang.
These activities provide the PLA with strong incentives to increase intelligence collection east of Taiwan. Through close-in reconnaissance, Beijing can seek to gather technical and operational data on Taiwan’s emerging capabilities, including new unmanned systems, missile deployments, force movements, and joint operational procedures.
Conclusion: The Battle for Taiwan’s East
For Taiwan, recent PLA activity suggests that the eastern side of the island can no longer be treated simply as a protected rear area.
Taiwan’s deployments during this year’s Han Kuang exercise already indicate a response to the PLA’s growing operational focus on the region. In addition to increasing naval and air patrols east of the island, Taiwan has begun deploying missile units to Orchid Island.
Orchid Island is located relatively close to the Philippines’ Batanes Islands, creating potential space for closer Philippines-Taiwan security cooperation. If combined with Japan’s southwestern islands — particularly Ishigaki and Yonaguni to Taiwan’s northeast — these locations could form important nodes in a broader defensive network along the First Island Chain. Such a network would not necessarily depend on the large-scale forward deployment of naval forces. Instead, it could emphasize an “anti-sea from land” approach, using distributed land-based missiles, sensors, UAVs, and intelligence networks deployed across strategically located islands.
The objective would be to turn geography into an operational advantage. By integrating Taiwan, the Batanes, and Japan’s southwestern islands into a more resilient surveillance and strike architecture, Taiwan and its partners could complicate PLA naval operations in the waters east of the island and partially offset China’s numerical superiority at sea.
The strategic competition over Taiwan is therefore increasingly extending beyond the Taiwan Strait itself. The waters east of Taiwan – linking the First Island Chain to the broader Western Pacific – are becoming an increasingly important operational theater. For Taiwan, the next major challenge may not be defending its western coastline, but ensuring that its eastern flank remains open, survivable, and connected to the wider Western Pacific.

Mother seeks justice 7 months after Thai-Swedish son’s fatal crash in Pattaya
The grieving family of 15-year-old Tommy Boulanger accuses police of failing to execute an arrest warrant seven months after the fatal crash
The mother of a 15-year-old Thai-Swedish teenager who died after his motorbike crashed into a truck illegally reversing into oncoming traffic has made an emotional appeal for justice, accusing police of failing to execute an arrest warrant for the alleged driver, a Chinese national, seven months after the fatal crash.
Tommy Boulanger, an aspiring footballer, was left in a coma following the February 20 crash in the Nongpure district of Chonburi, near the resort city of Pattaya. He never regained consciousness and died six days later.
Widely circulated CCTV footage of the crash shows a pickup truck reversing onto the main road without indicating – in an apparent attempt to make a U-turn outside a karaoke bar – leaving Tommy unable to brake in time before slamming into the back of the vehicle.
Tommy’s death has gripped the Thai public, reviving complaints over the country’s often sclerotic justice system and fuelling a mounting sense that wealthy foreign nationals are able to gain preferential treatment.
The Pattaya Provincial Court issued an arrest warrant on March 2 for the suspect – whose name has not formally been released to the media, though he is believed to be well known locally – on charges of reckless driving causing death.
