- Pushilin added that Russian forces are encircling the city from the southwest and northeast.
Importance of Dobropolye
- In an interview with TASS, Pushilin emphasized that the main supply route for the Ukrainian garrison in Kramatorsk and Slavyansk runs through Dobropolye.

'Naxalites can't make law': Heated exchange between lawyers during Vande Mataram SC hearing
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-22
12:26:20 UTC
21:26:20 KST

SC hearing on Vande Mataram turns heated over 'Naxalites' remark
NEW DELHI: A heated exchange broke out between senior advocate S Muralidhar and solicitor general Tushar Mehta in the Supreme Court on Tuesday after Mehta referred to “Naxalites” during arguments in a case concerning Vande Mataram.Muralidhar, appearing for Carnatic musician T M Krishna, immediately objected to the expression and repeatedly asked Mehta to withdraw it.“Law-making is as per the Constitution. Law-making cannot be as per the Naxalites idea,” news agency PTI quoted Mehta saying. His remarks came after Muralidhar questioned the manner in which an amendment relating to the national song had been enacted.“The solicitor must withdraw the expression he just used now. This is going live. I don't want an expression of the solicitor going live. I strongly object. Let the Solicitor repeat the expression he used,” Muralidhar said.Mehta maintained that he was responding to Muralidhar’s objection to the decision-making process and said Parliament had enacted the law in accordance with the Constitution.“I do not want anyone to question...he says he is objecting to the decision-making.
It is as per the Constitution,” the solicitor general said.Muralidhar continued to press for a withdrawal of the remark.“He started it. Why is the Solicitor using this kind of an expression? This does not behove a law officer. I have never heard a law officer using this expression,” Muralidhar said.“You cannot challenge the Constitution,” Mehta responded.Justice Joymalya Bagchi said the exchange was creating “unnecessary tension and emotion”, while Chief Justice Surya Kant intervened and said the bench was examining only the legal issue of constitutional interpretation.“Decorum is expected of law officers,” Muralidhar said.The bench later sought the Centre’s response to Krishna’s petition challenging penal provisions relating to Vande Mataram. It also asked the government to keep in mind a 1986 judgment that protected children from penal action if they did not sing the national anthem.Muralidhar, however, raised the “Naxalites” remark again after the order was dictated and sought to place his protest on record.“The learned solicitor used an expression which does not behove a law officer. I have to register my strong protest,” he said.Justice Bagchi replied, “We have not taken note of the comments. We restrict ourselves to the Constitutional issue.”Mehta said he was not apologetic and repeated his position.“I can repeat what I said. He said he is objecting to the way in which the decision-making was done. Decision-making was by the Parliament. I said that is the constitutional way, and not what the Naxalites want. I am not sorry about it,” the solicitor general said.Muralidhar accused Mehta of “playing to the gallery” and again protested.“Your lordships will not encourage this from a law officer,” he said.“Save your arguments for the next date,” the CJI told him.Senior advocate Sanjay Hegde, who was present in court for another matter, then intervened, saying, “To have a mind of one's own is not to be a Naxalite.”Justice Bagchi said that even if someone was labelled a Naxalite, that person would not lose their constitutional rights.Mehta clarified that he was not labelling any individual a Naxalite but was referring to an ideology.After Muralidhar left and the court moved to the next matter, Justice Bagchi returned to the issue while addressing Mehta.“I tell you, at least from my personal experience, we have continuously fought against extra-constitutional forces, both as members of the bar and of the bench. Our survival and our justification with the Constitution is to defeat these forces,” Justice Bagchi said.He stressed the importance of constitutional courts and due process, saying even people accused of terrorism were entitled to equal constitutional rights and fair trials.“Why will people come to courts and not to kangaroo courts? There are kangaroo courts. Constitutional courts have the respect and credibility. Why? Because we feel, even alleged terrorists, must have equal rights,” Justice Bagchi said.Mehta reiterated that he was referring to people who did not believe in constitutional decision-making.“Solicitor, we have not taken note of the comments,” Justice Bagchi said.
“I don't know why he took it personally,” Mehta said.
What was the Vande Mataram case about?
The bench, comprising CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, was hearing Krishna’s petition challenging penal protection given to Vande Mataram.During the hearing, Muralidhar argued that the amendment had been enacted without adequate public discussion or efforts to build a broader national consensus.“Ideally, these things should evolve as the building up of a public opinion,” he said, arguing against a “top down approach” to law-making.The court sought the Centre’s response to the plea and asked the government to consider the 1986 judgment concerning the national anthem while responding to the petition.

Her work brings together reportage and analysis, tracking developments in India and abroad while examining the broader social and economic currents shaping public discourse.

Talks over Saudi deposit in Egypt's bank amid Iran, Yemen wars
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-22
12:25:23 UTC
21:25:23 KST

Breadcrumb
Egypt seeks to keep $5.4 billion Saudi deposit as regional wars bite
The Egyptian government is holding talks with Saudi authorities to reach an agreement to renew a $5.434 billion Saudi deposit at the Central Bank of Egypt, due for repayment in October, or convert it into direct investments instead of allowing it to leave Egypt when it falls due.
Economic sources told The New Arab that high-level talks are taking place between the two countries, aimed at reaching an agreement to address implementation difficulties that have persisted since July 2026.
The difficulties are linked to the worsening impact of the ongoing war in the Gulf and Yemen on the Saudi economy.
At the same time, Egypt is trying to keep the Saudi deposit at the Central Bank so that it remains part of its foreign currency reserves, enabling the country to deal with the repercussions of the war in the Gulf and Bab al-Mandeb, which are increasing as shipping and import costs rise and Suez Canal revenues decline.
Egypt also faces difficulties in obtaining concessional foreign loans after interest rates on the dollar and major currencies increased.
Deposits and IMF guarantees
Financing and investment expert Wael al-Nahhas said the Saudi deposit due in October is renewed periodically and is among Saudi medium- and short-term deposits.
He said that the deposit, originally worth $5.3 billion, is linked annually to a dollar return, raising its value at maturity to about $5.434 billion.
He explained that despite intensive talks between Saudi and Egyptian authorities over converting the value of these deposits into direct investments, the two sides have not yet reached decisive results regarding their fate.
Nahhas told The New Arab that the Saudi deposits were provided to Egypt as part of guarantees offered by the International Monetary Fund when it signed its latest agreement with Egypt in 2024, which provides for $18.3 billion in cash support from Gulf states that cannot be withdrawn before the end of the Extended Fund Facility programme, which runs until December 2026.
There are exceptions related to the purchase of stakes or shares in public assets offered under the asset sale programme approved by the fund. The foreign currency proceeds from deposits or purchases must also remain in the central bank's reserves.
This means the continuation of Gulf deposits was part of the guarantees for financing the fund's programme and not a separate banking arrangement.
Al-Nahhas pointed out that the failure to reach an agreement between Egypt and Saudi Arabia on the future of the first part, which represents more than 50% of the Saudi deposit at the central bank, just weeks before it falls due, is raising many concerns within the banking sector.
Banking sector's view
An investment expert at a state-owned bank said Saudi Arabia had previously announced in 2024 that it intended to convert its deposits at the central bank into investments to support the economy, similar to what Qatar and the UAE had done through investments in real estate and tourism projects on the Mediterranean coast.
The aim is to circulate Gulf capital within Egypt rather than allow it to leave, and help Cairo avoid the departure of Gulf deposits while also avoiding presenting them as debt that must be repaid in the state budget. In turn, this eases pressure on external debt and the Egyptian pound, which is weakening as the dollar rises in value and hot money leaves government debt instruments.
The banking expert told The New Arab that Saudi Arabia's failure to announce its final position on the $5.434 billion deposit due in October, as well as the other deposit due for repayment in 2027, is normal.
The matter can be settled at the last moment before the maturity date, as happened in previous years, when approvals came through central bank channels directly from the Saudi Arabian Monetary Authority (the Saudi central bank).
The agreement was then announced after it had been implemented.
Al-Nahhas, however, believes that the delay in announcing the future of the Saudi deposit is linked to political and economic calculations that have emerged recently, such as the Houthis escalating attacks against Saudi oil facilities and the country facing difficulties exporting oil, with the possibility of exports to Europe being halted during October.
This threatens to reduce the kingdom's hard currency revenues at a time when it is looking for resources to purchase alternative oil deals that would enable it to engineer oil deals for international markets, and places additional financial burdens on the kingdom, making it dependent of its external deposits for repayment.
Restrictions on foreign investment
Al-Nahhas noted that economic pressures had prompted Saudi authorities to issue a decision restricting the foreign investments of public money market funds, particularly in emerging markets exposed to risks, and will push the funds to rearrange their portfolios during a transition period of up to two years.
He explained that although the decision issued last week by the Saudi Capital Market Authority does not extend to the strategic investments of the Public Investment Fund or Saudi companies operating in Egypt, it requires funds whose foreign investments exceed 5% to regularise their positions within no more than two years, and includes not making, entering into or renewing any transaction that would keep the ratio above 5%.
Investments that exceed 20% of their net assets must reduce them to below 20% within six months, and must then complete the procedures to regularise their positions and reach the 5% ceiling.
In its latest report on the seventh review of the Egyptian economy, issued on 13 August 2026, the International Monetary Fund acknowledged that financing, debt and inflation risks remain high despite the Egyptian economy having overcome the initial shock of the US-Israeli war on Iran.
It said any regional escalation could once again put strong pressure on the dollar, reserves and growth.
The fund believes public debt is sustainable over the medium term, but not with a high degree of probability, as risks of sovereign stress remain.
Article translated from Arabic by Afrah Almatwari. To read the original, click here.

Ukraine Strikes Russian Drone Base in Oryol, Hits Five Launchers and Storage Facilities
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-22
12:25:12 UTC
21:25:12 KST

- Category
- War in Ukraine
Ukraine Strikes Russian Drone Base in Oryol, Hits Five Launchers and Storage Facilities
Ukrainian forces struck a Russian storage and launch site for attack drones in Russia’s Oryol region, damaging five launchers and several storage facilities, Ukraine’s General Staff reported on September 22.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
According to the General Staff, the strike was carried out on September 21 against a facility near the settlement of Tsymbulova, which was used by Russian forces to store, prepare, and launch attack drones.
At least three drone storage facilities were hit, resulting in fires at the site. The strike also damaged a launch area used for jet-powered UAVs, as well as five drone launchers.
The General Staff said Ukrainian forces systematically target facilities used to store, prepare, and launch Russian attack drones as part of efforts to reduce Moscow’s ability to conduct strikes against civilian targets in Ukraine.
The operation follows a series of Ukrainian strikes against other Russian military assets. On September 20 and overnight into September 21, Ukrainian forces targeted a Kasta radar system valued at at least $60 million, as well as a drone command post and an area where Russian troops were concentrated.
Ukraine’s General Staff reported that the radar was struck near Pikuzy in the temporarily occupied Donetsk region. The system was identified as a Kasta-2E2 (39N6), a mobile radar designed to detect low-flying aircraft, missiles, and unmanned aerial vehicles at ranges of up to 150 kilometers.
Ukrainian strikes have also targeted Russia’s oil infrastructure. A fire broke out at the Kuibyshev Oil Refinery in Russia’s Samara region following an overnight Ukrainian drone attack on September 22, with preliminary analysis suggesting that one of the facility’s processing units was damaged, Russian media outlet ASTRA reported.
Residents of the Samara region reported hearing explosions overnight. After analyzing eyewitness footage, ASTRA identified the Kuibyshev refinery as the apparent target, with footage showing a fire at the facility.

Putin to Attend China APEC Summit, Skipping Trump’s G20 in US
Unknown

- Category

Putin to Attend China APEC Summit, Skipping Trump’s G20 in US
Russian leader Vladimir Putin plans to travel to China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit hosted by Chinese leader Xi Jinping in November, while a trip to the G20 summit hosted by US President Donald Trump is considered highly unlikely.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
According to Bloomberg on September 21, people familiar with the Kremlin’s plans said Putin intends to attend the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting in person for the first time since 2017. The summit is scheduled for November 18–19 in Shenzhen, China. The official APEC schedule confirms those dates.
The Kremlin has not formally announced Putin’s participation in either summit. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov declined to comment on the plans, Bloomberg reported.
Russian officials have previously discussed the possibility of a three-way meeting involving Putin, Xi and Trump on the sidelines of APEC.
Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov said in early September that Putin and Xi had discussed such a possibility, though any meeting would depend on whether Trump travels to China.
Bloomberg reported that Putin has generally avoided major multilateral gatherings where he could encounter European leaders supporting Ukraine, as well as representatives of Canada, Japan, South Korea and Australia.
Russian officials are also considering the possibility that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy could attend the G20 gathering, according to the outlet.
The G20 Leaders’ Summit is scheduled for December 14–15 at Trump National Doral Miami in Florida.
People familiar with the Kremlin’s thinking told Bloomberg that Russian officials do not expect substantial progress in negotiations over Russia’s war against Ukraine before the G20 summit. The outlet also reported growing frustration in Moscow with Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.
Putin and Trump last met in Alaska on August 15, 2025.
Since the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Putin has also traveled to countries including China, India, the United Arab Emirates, North Korea and Vietnam.
If Putin attends the Shenzhen meeting, it would mark his first in-person appearance at an APEC leaders’ summit since 2017, according to Bloomberg. China is hosting APEC for the third time, with the 2026 leaders’ meeting centered on openness, innovation and regional cooperation.
Putin’s international travel has been complicated by sanctions, security considerations and an International Criminal Court arrest warrant issued in 2023 over the unlawful deportation and transfer of Ukrainian children. Despite the warrant, Putin traveled to Mongolia in 2024, even though the country is a party to the Rome Statute establishing the ICC.
Earlier, the UK said the so-called “Anchorage compromise,” which Russia claimed involved US acceptance of Ukrainian territorial concessions and abandoning NATO aspirations, was “firmly dead.” The alleged understanding was linked to the August 2025 summit between Trump and Putin in Alaska.

U.S. Army tests drone mothership that launches its own swarm
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-22
12:24:09 UTC
21:24:09 KST

- The U.S. Army's XVIII Airborne Corps tested Modalic's Autonomous Swarm Mothership drone during Scarlet Dragon 26-3 at Fort Bragg, North Carolina, in September.
- The exercise used swarms of up to 100 drones to test whether sensors, software and defenses could track and defeat saturation aerial attacks.
The U.S. Army’s XVIII Airborne Corps evaluated a drone mothership built by Modalic during Scarlet Dragon 26-3, an experimentation exercise held at Fort Bragg, North Carolina, in mid-September.
The aircraft, called the Autonomous Swarm Mothership, launched smaller drones in flight as soldiers tested whether the network could track the parent aircraft, separate its daughter drones, and identify the larger threat as multiple aerial contacts appeared.
The demonstration was part of a broader test of counter-drone systems at Scarlet Dragon 26-3, which ran drone swarms of up to 100 aircraft to stress sensor networks, battle-management software, and air-defense crews. Soldiers evaluated whether sensors, artificial intelligence tools, electronic warfare, autonomous systems, and defensive weapons could work together against saturation attacks, rather than testing each system on its own.
Modalic showed a production version of its mothership aircraft, called Chariot, at the same event. Company co-founder and CEO Zack Fishbein told reporters at Fort Bragg on Sept. 16 that Chariot weighs 200 pounds (91 kg) and carries a payload of up to 100 pounds (45 kg), with flight testing on the new aircraft set to begin in November.
“The Scarlet Dragon exercise has become a validation exercise in the dirt with Soldiers doing integrated, real-world operational-type tasks,” said Col. Tom Monahan, director of the XVIII Airborne Corps’ Joint Innovation Outpost.
Scarlet Dragon is the Corps’ recurring series of field exercises that pairs soldiers with industry partners to test emerging technology under realistic conditions. This was the third iteration in the current cycle, following events in December 2025 and earlier this year, each expanding on lessons from the last. An August event at Fort Bragg’s Joint Innovation Outpost drew more than 50 companies to test counter-drone sensors ahead of the September exercise.
Beyond the Modalic mothership, the exercise tested a dual-mode air-ground light tactical vehicle built on an off-road utility terrain vehicle chassis, evaluated for its ability to shift between ground mobility and flight without relying on runways or fixed infrastructure, with potential uses in reconnaissance, resupply, and casualty evacuation. Soldiers also launched small unmanned aircraft systems in coordinated swarms from a single site at Holland Drop Zone to test their ability to fly in formation.
The Corps plans to continue testing these technologies during Scarlet Dragon 27-1 in April 2027, ahead of a larger exercise called Summit Strike at Fort Drum, New York, in September 2027. The Army has not disclosed whether it plans to procure the Modalic mothership or set a timeline for fielding any of the systems tested at Fort Bragg.

IGIA immigration lapse: ‘Entire hub, spoke ecosystem strengthened now,’ says Naidu

Reiterating India’s goal to become a global aviation hub
NEW DELHI: Union aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu Tuesday said authorities have learnt from the recent immigration lapse at Delhi Airport where three hub and spoke passengers of Air India flew from Amritsar to Germany via Delhi without clearing immigration and taking corrective steps to ensure such an incident never recurs. Reiterating India’s goal to become a global aviation hub, the minister said hub and spoke will be expanded to more airports while plugging all gaps to create a foolproof seamless system.“There should be no compromise with security detail in our airport operations. We want convenient and seamless international transfers. That is where hub and spoke comes in. India truly believes in becoming a global hub. So far three airports have hub and spoke and we will expand this list. There was a lapse. The aviation ministry responded and issued a show cause to AI so that any security related issue should be addressed,” Naidu said.Authorities met AI officials and “understood the checks and balances that have been put in place. Now there are multiple parameters in place to ensure this does not recut. Things have settled down. We have created a robust ecosystem. This lapse has been an understanding for us,” he added.
The feedback to the hub and spoke with passengers clearing customs and immigration at the local spoke airport has been “great”. “This has led to convenience to passengers, especially for women traveling with children and connecting domestic to international at Delhi late at night,” the minister said.The Union aviation ministry had issued a show cause notice to Air India for lapses that saw three foreigners fly into Delhi from Amritsar on Sept 4 and then within an hour depart for Munich on a codeshare Lufthansa flight without the mandatory immigration check. “Air India personnel who were to escort passengers through respective pathways were found to be at fault and they were immediately suspended. Have created multiple systems now; the role digi yatra role plays; how passengers move at connecting airports. The ecosystem has been strengthened,” Naidu said.

Media should pool efforts to combat virus of deepfakes — OANA Secretary General
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-22
12:21:36 UTC
21:21:36 KST

MOSCOW, September 22. /TASS/. Deepfakes have become a "virus of the digital age," making it essential for media organizations to maintain an ongoing dialogue about methods and best practices for detecting and combating them, Marat Abulkhatin, Secretary General of the Organization of Asia-Pacific News Agencies (OANA) and Deputy Director General of TASS, said.
"Deepfakes - the virus of the digital age - deserve special attention: they spread rapidly, are difficult to detect without specialized technology, are constantly evolving to become increasingly convincing, and adapt to modern detection tools," he said at the Dialogue on Fakes 4.0 international forum. "To build a robust system for exchanging reliable information, it is necessary not only to develop our own methodologies and approaches, but also to share them."
Abulkhatin noted that technological advances had created a wide range of tools capable of distorting information and falsifying facts. At the same time, he said, new digital solutions had emerged to help identify information sources and verify data and the origins of content.
Against this backdrop, he highlighted TASS’s extensive network of experts, which he described as a "unique database" built up over the years. It includes press services of ministries, government agencies, universities and regional authorities, as well as medical professionals, scientists, educators, lawyers and economists.
Personal responsibility and technology
"TASS’s experience shows that countering fakes does not begin with refuting information that has already circulated, but much earlier - with an editorial culture of verifying every single report," Abulkhatin said.
In his view, effective efforts to combat disinformation require combining technological capabilities with the personal "responsibility of each journalist and editorial team for the final decision to publish."
"It is precisely the combination of professional responsibility, multi-level verification, and modern technologies that makes it possible to maintain high-quality information," Abulkhatin concluded.
About the forum
The Dialogue about Fakes 4.0 forum is a global platform for discussing methods to combat disinformation and develop fact-checking technologies. The event is taking place at the Russia National Center with the participation of over 2,000 journalists, experts and businesspeople from 80 countries. It is organized by the Global Fact-Checking Network (GFCN), established in 2025 by the TASS news agency, the autonomous nonprofit organization "Dialogue Regions," and the New Media Workshop. TASS is the forum’s strategic media partner.

Pedro Sánchez advocates for universal and inclusive multilateralism in the face of attempts to dismantle the rules-based order
President's News - 2026.9.22
United Nations Headquarters, New York (United States)
Pool Moncloa/Borja Puig de la Bellacasa
The President of the Government of Spain, Pedro Sánchez, began his participation in the United Nations High-Level Week with a speech at the 'Partners for Multilateralism (P4M)' event, organised by the president of the European Council together with the leaders of Canada and Kenya. In his speech, the head of the Executive defended universal and inclusive multilateralism in the face of attempts to dismantle the rules-based order.
The President of the Government of Spain explained that 'coalitions of like-minded countries' are frequently formed, which work within small groups to find solutions to urgent problems. In light of this reality, he argued that "the response to a fragmented world cannot be further fragmentation" because peace, he said, "does not come from narrowing the circle of trust, but from widening it".
Pool Moncloa/Borja Puig de la Bellacasa
In his speech, Pedro Sánchez emphasised that "Spain remains firmly committed to multilateralism" through its opposition to war and its commitment to diplomacy, by championing sustainable development and a fairer international financial architecture, as well as by supporting "more inclusive and more legitimate" multilateral institutions that give a voice "to those who have historically been marginalised".

How to use a seized account during martial law
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-22
15:20:29 EEST
21:20:29 KST

How to use a seized account during martial law
Kyiv • UNN
A debtor may choose one seized account and spend up to UAH 17,294 per month. To do so, they must submit an application to the enforcement officer.
Seizure of funds in bank accounts is one of the mechanisms for the compulsory enforcement of decisions concerning a debtor. If a person does not comply with a decision voluntarily, a state or private enforcement officer may restrict their ability to dispose of their money and direct the funds toward repayment of the debt. At the same time, the law establishes a number of exceptions. For example, during martial law, people are allowed to use a specified amount from one seized account.
What needs to be done to use such funds was determined by UNN.
When money in an account may be seized
To compulsorily collect money from the accounts of a person who owes a debt, the relevant authorities must initiate enforcement proceedings. The Law of Ukraine "On Enforcement Proceedings" provides for the compulsory enforcement of requirements set out in:
-  writs of execution; 
-  court decisions; 
-  separate rulings and resolutions of courts,  
-  other documents recognized by law as enforceable.  
This refers to a mechanism that may be applied to various types of debt after legal grounds for compulsory enforcement have arisen.
After enforcement proceedings are initiated, the enforcement officer sends inquiries to banks to determine what funds the debtor has. The debt will primarily be recovered from the person's funds in hryvnias and foreign currency. However, the financial seizure may also extend to funds deposited into the accounts after the resolution is issued.
In addition, the law provides for the possibility of seizing electronic money and other specified assets of the debtor.
At the same time, only the amount of funds specified in the rulings of the relevant authorities may be recovered. However, it is worth emphasizing that this amount includes not only the "principal" of the debt. The person will also have to pay:
-  the enforcement fee;  
-  the costs of the enforcement proceedings;  
-  fines; 
-  the basic remuneration of the private enforcement officer.  
All this applies only in cases provided for by law.
What funds cannot be recovered to repay a debt
The list of funds that the State Enforcement Service (SES) cannot recover from a person to pay a debt is established by law. These include certain social and compensatory payments:
-  maternity benefits; 
-  a one-time childbirth allowance; 
-  adoption assistance; 
-  payments for children placed under guardianship or custody, etc. 
Certain employee compensations are also not subject to recovery, for example, those related to an official business trip or transfer to work in another area. The law separately prohibits the seizure of funds in accounts with a special-use regime and other accounts for which a direct prohibition on recovery has been established. If a bank receives a resolution to seize such an account, it must notify the enforcement officer of the relevant restrictions.
In practice, it is important for a debtor not to limit themselves to informing the bank that the money is of social origin. If payments protected by law have been seized, it is advisable to obtain supporting documents confirming the purpose and origin of the funds and submit them to the enforcement officer.
When the seizure must be lifted from an account
One of the main grounds for lifting the seizure from an account and unblocking it is the full fulfillment of the requirements of the enforcement document and payment of the amount necessary to satisfy the claimants' demands, the enforcement fee, the costs of the proceedings, and fines provided for by law.
In addition, the seizure of funds may be lifted if the SES receives information that the account has a special-use regime or that the funds in question are specifically funds whose recovery is prohibited by law. However, as we have already noted above, the SES / private enforcement officer must receive the relevant documents for this. In such a case, the seizure of the account must be lifted on the day following the day on which the relevant agency received these documents.
The seizure of accounts may also be canceled if the enforcement officer violates the procedure itself.
Please note: if a person considers the actions or inaction of an enforcement officer to be unlawful, they have the right to challenge them. In matters concerning the enforcement of a court decision, a complaint may be filed with the court that issued the enforcement document. Actions taken during the enforcement of decisions by other bodies may be challenged in an administrative court in accordance with the procedure established by law.
How much money can be used from an account under arrest during martial law
Even if the State Enforcement Service has frozen funds because of debts, a person may continue to spend money, taking into account the martial law in the country. However, they will have to choose only one bank account for this purpose. In addition, taxes and fees may be paid from it, regardless of the fact that it is under arrest.
However, even such an account will be subject to a limit: each month, it will be possible to use an amount not exceeding two minimum wages established by the state budget law as of January 1 of the relevant year. Currently, this amounts to UAH 17,294.
How to designate an account for expenditure transactions
The debtor must apply to the state or private enforcement officer handling the enforcement proceedings with a request to designate one current account. The application must specify the account number in the IBAN format and the name of the bank where it is held. After reviewing the application, the enforcement officer issues a resolution designating the current account for expenditure transactions. Once the bank receives this resolution, it allows transactions up to the amount established by law.
Please note: even if a person's accounts are frozen at several banks, only one of them may be designated for such transactions. The same rule applies if several enforcement proceedings have been opened against the debtor simultaneously: one current account is designated for all of them.
For example, having three enforcement proceedings does not mean that the debtor will receive three separate limits of UAH 17,294 each. The total available amount in 2026 remains capped at two minimum wages per month.
What to do if an account has been frozen
First of all, it is worth finding out who imposed the freeze and within which enforcement proceedings. The bank itself often provides this information in its mobile application.
After that, the amount of the debt and the grounds for collection must be verified.
If the debt exists but the person needs access to money for everyday expenses, during martial law they may apply to the enforcement officer with a request to designate one account for expenditure transactions. If funds that may not be subject to collection by law have been frozen, it is necessary to obtain documents confirming their origin or the account's special status and submit them to the enforcement officer with a request to lift the freeze.
After the debt has been fully repaid, it is also worth checking whether the enforcement officer issued the relevant resolution and whether the bank received it.

Earlier, the Ministry of Justice explained which property cannot be seized during enforcement proceedings.

- US Secretary Marco Rubio expressed openness to diplomacy but warned of Iran's hardline leadership under Supreme Leader Khamenei, insisting Iran cannot have nuclear weapons.
- Gulf states seek regional security talks, with a Qatari proposal for a security framework including Iran; meanwhile, Saudi Arabia faces increased threats from Houthi advances affecting oil exports.
AI generated
DUBAI – Iran and the United States hinted on Sept 22 at the prospect of reviving negotiations to end their conflict, with the presidents of both countries due at the UN General Assembly in New York.
The general debate will be the first event attended by both US President Donald Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian since Trump launched Operation Epic Fury, alongside Israel, against Iran in February.
Trump had said on Sept 20 he would be open to meeting the Iranian President.
A senior Iranian official said there were no plans for the two leaders to meet directly, but that Iran’s delegation had full authority to revive talks.
Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz to Gulf shipping within seven days if the US fulfilled Tehran’s demands to ease military pressure and lift an American blockade on Iranian ports, the Iranian official said.
The official added that Iran had conveyed its latest proposal to Washington via mediators last week.
“The US needs to announce that it wants to resolve the issue diplomatically, make that official, and then agree on a timeline for how the process will move forward,” the official said. “The UN General Assembly is a golden opportunity for the US to return to diplomacy.”
Secretary of State Marco Rubio told NBC’s Today show the US was open to speaking with the Iranians, “especially if it has the prospects of leading to something positive and ultimately achieving the goal of what this is all about”.
No face-to-face meetings between Iran and the United States are known to have taken place since July, when an agreement on an interim deal to end the war collapsed just weeks after it was signed by Trump and Pezeshkian.
Asked by news programme Fox And Friends about the prospect of a meeting between the presidents, Rubio said of Trump: “He’s a businessman who comes from the world of practicality and common sense. And common sense tells you there’s no harm in engaging and talking to someone.”
Reminders of hardline positions
“The central issue here is Iran is run by lunatic clerics,” Rubio told Fox, noting that Pezeshkian is subordinate under Iran’s ruling system to Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei.
“The Supreme Leader is a radical Shia cleric and we need to remember that when we talk,” he said, adding that “these people can never have nuclear weapons”.
In a reminder of Iran’s firm position so far, Parliament Speaker Mohammed Baqer Qalibaf, who headed Iran’s negotiating team at previous talks, said on Sept 22 that Iran would never surrender.
“Trump must understand that he cannot impose his power on the Iranian people and its armed forces,” he said.
Trump is due to meet on Sept 22 leaders of the six Gulf Arab states: Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.
The Gulf countries are keen to restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz but wary of giving their longstanding rival Iran too much power. All apart from Oman also host huge US military bases that have come under repeated Iranian attack throughout the war.
Saudis increasingly exposed to effects of war
The biggest of them, Saudi Arabia, has been drawn deeper into the war in September, with Houthi fighters aligned to Iran advancing in Yemen, routing forces of a Saudi-backed government there and threatening Saudi oil exports through the Red Sea.
There was some relief on oil markets on Sept 22, after sources told Reuters that Saudi Arabia had restarted operations at its East-West Pipeline and could resume exports within hours, albeit at reduced volume, from the Red Sea port of Yanbu.
The pipeline, Saudi Arabia’s main alternative route for exports to bypass wartime disruption in the Strait of Hormuz, was shut down after attacks on Sept 10 that Riyadh blamed on Iranian allies in Iraq.
The Houthis have pushed back Saudi-supported government forces with the aim of controlling the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, the southern mouth of the Red Sea, and have attacked Saudi Arabia directly with missiles and drones.
The US, which bombed the Houthis for two months in 2025, has so far rebuffed repeated pleas from Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to rejoin the fight against the group.
The New York Times reported that Trump called off US strikes against the Houthis on Sept 20 at the last minute after troops had already begun loading bombs onto planes.
Asked why Washington had so far held back from striking the Houthis, Rubio said: “Ultimately, if it comes down to it, the United States will always stand with Saudi Arabia and support them because we have an agreement with them to do so.
“That said, that is a very dangerous and complex conflict that pre-exists... We have a history with the Houthis as well, and that’s something we don’t want to see impacted either.”
Qatari proposal on the table
On the table at the Gulf states’ meeting with Trump is a Qatari proposal for a framework to bring Iran and the six states into a common security architecture, regional sources said.
Speaking at a Qatar Economic Forum in New York on Sept 20, Qatari Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani said any such arrangement would need to provide security guarantees for the Gulf states and expand economic interdependence with Iran.
“Lasting security cannot be built through repeated cycles of escalations and retaliation, or arrangements that leave any state permanently exposed to insecurity,” he said. REUTERS

Hong Kong to bar firms with integrity offences from building renovation lists

Hong Kong to bar firms with integrity offences from building renovation lists
Secretary for Development Bernadette Linn says applications to pre-qualify will open next Wednesday and lists rolled out by year-end
Hong Kong building maintenance consultants and contractors prosecuted or convicted of integrity-related offences in the past three years will be excluded from pre-qualified lists set up for owners undertaking renovation projects, the development minister has said.
Secretary for Development Bernadette Linn Hon-ho said on Tuesday that applications to join the lists – covering inspection consultants, supervision consultants and building works contractors – would open next Wednesday and close on October 23. The lists would be set up by the end of the year, she added.
Linn told the Legislative Council’s development panel that the lists would be reviewed every two years, as authorities tightened oversight of integrity standards.
“If they are convicted of integrity-related offences, they will be removed from the pre-qualified lists immediately,” Linn said.

22 September 2026, New York – The Republic of Moldova and the Togolese Republic have officially established diplomatic relations. A document to this effect was signed in New York by the Foreign Ministers of the two countries, Mihai Popșoi and Robert Dussey.
The Republic of Moldova and the Togolese Republic thus affirmed their commitment to developing bilateral relations in accordance with the principles of international law and the Charter of the United Nations, with full respect for the sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of both states.
During their discussions, the two ministers highlighted the importance of interinstitutional cooperation between the Republic of Moldova and the Togolese Republic, as well as cooperation in sectors of mutual interest. The officials expressed confidence that the establishment of diplomatic relations would facilitate Moldova–Togo contacts and open up new opportunities for cooperation between the two countries.

Later today in New York, a document establishing diplomatic relations between the Republic of Moldova and the Republic of Namibia is also due to be signed.
The establishment of diplomatic relations with Togo and Namibia is part of the Republic of Moldova’s efforts to expand dialogue and cooperation with UN Member States and strengthen its international partnerships.

Ukraine attacks radiation monitor at Europe’s largest nuclear power plant
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-22
12:15:43 UTC
21:15:43 KST

Ukraine attacks radiation monitor at Europe’s largest nuclear power plant
A Ukrainian drone strike has damaged a radiation monitoring post near the Zaporozhye Nuclear Power Plant, the facility said on Tuesday.
The station was located near the village of Ivanovka, around 13 km from the nuclear plant, and formed part of the system used to track radiation levels in the surrounding area. Such posts regularly collect data on background radiation, allowing specialists to detect changes and respond quickly if conditions deteriorate.
The plant said the remaining monitoring equipment and capacity were sufficient to continue observing radiation levels, but noted that the loss of the station has reduced the amount of data that could be quickly gathered from that particular area.
In the event of an emergency, the loss could become significant as specialists would need reliable readings from multiple locations to determine the nature and scale of any changes in radiation levels.
At the same time, the facility stressed that losing one post did not mean radiation monitoring had stopped and did not itself indicate any radiation threat.
Nevertheless, it warned that further attacks on radiation monitoring infrastructure could reduce specialists’ ability to obtain information quickly and comprehensively in the event of an emergency.
Tuesday’s strike follows a series of attacks on and around the ZNPP that Moscow has blamed on Ukraine. Earlier this month, the Russian nuclear corporation Rosatom said Ukrainian strikes hit tankers delivering emergency diesel fuel to the plant, killing two Russian servicemen and wounding several others. The fuel is used to power the backup generators needed for critical safety systems if the facility loses its external electricity supply.
In July, a drone strike on a service vehicle near the plant’s industrial site also killed ZNPP chief engineer Aleksandr Yakovlev and his driver. Rosatom has accused Ukrainian forces of using drones to scatter anti-personnel mines on roads used by plant employees and residents of nearby Energodar.
Russia has repeatedly warned that continued attacks around the facility risk triggering a nuclear emergency with consequences extending beyond the immediate area.
Moscow has also criticized the International Atomic Energy Agency, which maintains a presence at the plant, for reporting explosions, drones and other military activity around the ZNPP without publicly identifying Ukraine as responsible.

U.S. Navy tests new tool to plan missions for autonomous jets
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-22
12:15:31 UTC
21:15:31 KST

- The U.S. Navy demonstrated its Collaborative Autonomy Mission Planning system during Gray Flag 2026 at Point Mugu Sea Range, using an MQ-20 Avenger surrogate aircraft.
- The system translates human-written mission plans into instructions autonomous aircraft can execute, and the Navy has not set a timeline for operational use.
The U.S. Navy demonstrated a new system for planning and controlling autonomous combat aircraft during Gray Flag 2026, a large-force test event held at Point Mugu Sea Range in California this month. The Navy calls the system Collaborative Autonomy Mission Planning, or CAMP.
The demonstration used a General Atomics MQ-20 Avenger acting as a surrogate autonomous aircraft. Navy engineers from the Strike Planning & Execution Systems office, known as PMX-281, built a mission plan, sent it to the aircraft, let it carry out the plan, and reviewed the results afterward.
CAMP is meant to fix a specific problem: mission planners plan strikes and patrols the same way they always have, using a system called the Collaborative Mission Planning Continuum, but autonomous aircraft need that information translated into a format they can act on. CAMP does that translation, converting a human-written plan into instructions an unmanned aircraft can execute as part of a larger mission alongside manned jets.
“CAMP is about making autonomy more usable by integrating into mission environments with both manned and unmanned platforms,” said Capt. Todd “Toby” Keith, the PMX-281 program manager. “This demonstration showed how we can connect the way operators plan missions today in the CMPC with the way autonomous aircraft will execute those missions. That can reduce the burden on our operators, improve interoperability and help bring collaborative autonomy closer to operational use.”
The Navy has not said when CAMP might reach operational units or how many aircraft it has been tested against beyond the single MQ-20 surrogate used at Point Mugu.
PMX-281 sits under the Program Executive Office for Unmanned Aviation and Strike Weapons and has spent recent months testing pieces of the Navy’s autonomy roadmap using surrogate aircraft rather than the eventual production platforms. In December 2025, the Navy and Shield AI flew two BQM-177A target drones under the direction of a simulated F/A-18 at the same Point Mugu range, using Shield AI’s Hivemind software to defend a patrol area against virtual adversaries in a live, virtual and constructive test environment. That effort, part of a program the Navy calls EPIC, focused on getting unmanned aircraft to fly and fight together. CAMP addresses a different piece of the puzzle: how a human planner’s intent gets translated into something an autonomous aircraft can execute in the first place.
The demonstration comes as the Navy works to define what its future carrier-based unmanned combat aircraft will actually look like. In late August, Naval Air Systems Command asked industry to propose designs for the first increment of the Navy’s own Collaborative Combat Aircraft program, seeking a carrier-launched, weaponized drone able to operate from Ford-class and Nimitz-class carriers alongside manned fighters, with a per-unit cost target of $30 million, The Defence Blog reported. Systems like CAMP are meant to work with whatever aircraft eventually wins that competition, since the mission-planning translation layer is built to be independent of any single autonomous platform or airframe.

The new structure will support joint efforts to strengthen multilateralism and promote the organisation’s values globally.
The event also provided an opportunity to reaffirm cooperation between the Republic of Moldova and the Council of Europe, particularly in implementing democratic reforms, including through the Action Plan for the Republic of Moldova 2025–2028, as well as in drawing on the organisation’s expertise to support the country’s European path.
Deputy Prime Minister Mihai Popșoi welcomed the opening of the Council of Europe’s Permanent Observer Office in New York and expressed confidence that it would contribute to effective cooperation between the organisations for the benefit of their member states.

The Nicaraguan government is responsible for at least eight deaths in custody since it began its crackdown on dissent and assault of democratic institutions in 2018, UN experts said Tuesday.
The report from the UN Group of Human Rights Experts on Nicaragua was the latest condemnation of the government of married co-Presidents Daniel Ortega and Rosario Murillo, which has crushed dissent since 2018 mass protests and recently cancelled elections.
“A State that resorts to enforced disappearance and allows persons to die in its custody falls short of the minimum human rights standards required for credible democratic governance,” said Jan-Michael Simon, the group’s chair.
The report detailed inconsistencies in the government’s account of the in-custody death of Indigenous Miskito leader Brooklyn Rivera, who was imprisoned for 32 months with almost no contact with his family before he died in May.

Zurich poses highest risk of property bubble in the world

Zurich poses highest risk of property bubble in the world
Among the world's cities, Zurich poses the highest risk of a property bubble, ahead of Tokyo, says a new analysis by Swiss bank UBS. In Geneva, the risk has increased compared with last year.
With an index reading of 1.69 points, up from 1.55 points last year, Zurich tops the list of cities with the highest risk of a property market bubble, according to the Global Real Estate Bubble Index published on Tuesday by Switzerland’s leading bank.
Over the past 20 years, Switzerland’s biggest city has seen the sharpest rise in property prices of all the cities surveyed. Its appeal as a business hub and the influx of international professionals, particularly in the technology and artificial intelligence (AI) sectors, are driving demand for housing.
+ Zero interest rates drive up Swiss property prices
At the same time, low interest rates and a marked shortage of supply are putting further pressure on prices: the vacancy rate is close to zero. The supply of owner-occupied housing remains well below its historical level. Furthermore, affordability issues are widening the gap between the most sought-after neighbourhoods and the rest of the property market.
Tokyo and Miami are just behind Zurich in the rankings, with indices of 1.54 and 1.41 points respectively. Geneva, with an index of 1.12 points, also presents a high risk of a property bubble. In Geneva, the risks have increased compared with last year, when the index stood at 1.05 points.
+ Switzerland faces worst housing shortage since 2014
In contrast, Paris (0.33 points), London (0.30 points), New York (0.28 points), San Francisco (-0.02 points) and São Paulo (-0.24 points) show the lowest risks.
UBS analysed residential property prices in 23 international cities. Lisbon and Seoul were included in the study for the first time this year.

What will UK's Ed Miliband focus on at his first UNGA?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-22
12:13:34 UTC
21:13:34 KST

Breadcrumb
What will UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband focus on at his first UNGA?
UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband is attending his first United Nations General Assembly high-level week since taking office, arriving in New York with the Middle East and Sudan among the major crises confronting world leaders.
In his first nine weeks as foreign secretary, Miliband has already taken a tougher stance on Israel's illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank, announcing plans to ban imports from settlements and impose sanctions on individuals and companies involved in settlement activity.
But how will Britain's new foreign secretary approach these issues on the world stage? And where does he stand on other major questions facing this year's gathering, including the US-Israel war on Iran, Sudan's devastating civil war and nuclear disarmament?
Will Miliband discuss Israel and Palestine?
Israel and Palestine are expected to feature prominently in Miliband's diplomacy in New York.
Earlier this month, the UK announced plans to prohibit imports of goods from illegal Israeli settlements and introduce sanctions against individuals and companies supporting, facilitating or benefiting from settlement activity.
The measures followed Miliband's condemnation of settlement expansion and settler violence in the occupied West Bank. He has also repeatedly backed a two-state solution and said Israeli settlements are a "flagrant breach of international law".
However, Miliband has rejected the wider Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS) movement, drawing a distinction between measures targeting illegal settlements and a broader boycott of Israel.
Daniel Forti, the International Crisis Group's Head of UN Affairs, told The New Arab that Miliband "will be closely involved in discussions around Palestine and the Two State Solution, where UN-backed diplomacy has fallen by the wayside at the expense of the Board of Peace".
"States will watch closely to see how UK officials defend their sanctions on Israel for expanding settlements in the West Bank, and how fiery a response they receive from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu."
Netanyahu is also expected to attend this week's gathering in New York. He responded angrily to Britain's settlement measures, while the Israeli government has strongly rejected international pressure over its policies in the West Bank.
What about Sudan?
Sudan is also emerging as a significant part of Miliband's first UNGA agenda.
Britain is the UN Security Council penholder on Sudan and has pushed for stronger international action as the country's civil war and humanitarian crisis continue.
Speaking in New York on Monday, Miliband described Sudan as "the worst humanitarian crisis this century" and set out three priorities for international action: diplomacy aimed at securing a ceasefire and eventual civilian government, improved humanitarian access, and greater protection for civilians.
He also called for stronger scrutiny of countries and networks supplying weapons and other support that are fuelling the conflict.
Forti said Miliband would use his time in New York to raise the profile of the war.
"Miliband will also hope to use his time in New York [to] raise the profile of the on-going war in Sudan. The UK leads the Security Council's discussions on the country but has been unable to rally its members around a common strategy to back various diplomatic efforts," he said.
"The UK will likely use a range of side events during UNGA to remind world leaders of the war's horrific toll and the urgent need to bring the warring parties back to the negotiating table."
What has Miliband said about the war on Iran?
Miliband's response to the US-Israel-led war on Iran has combined calls for diplomacy with a focus on the conflict's economic impact on Britain.
Following talks with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Miliband said Britain would work towards a ceasefire, while repeatedly highlighting the consequences of instability in the Middle East and disruption to the Strait of Hormuz for energy prices and the cost of living in the UK.
He has also maintained Britain's longstanding position that Iran must not acquire a nuclear weapon.
In a foreign policy speech earlier this year, Miliband said the objective should be to move "from conflict to containment", using coordinated international action and diplomacy to prevent Iran from rebuilding capabilities that threaten regional states and international shipping.
Iran will also be represented at this week's meetings in New York, potentially making diplomacy surrounding the conflict another important issue on the sidelines of the General Assembly.
What is Miliband's stance on nuclear weapons?
Nuclear weapons will also be on the UN agenda this week, with a high-level meeting marking the International Day for the Total Elimination of Nuclear Weapons.
The meeting is intended to give UN member states an opportunity to reaffirm their commitment to nuclear disarmament.
Miliband has historically supported maintaining Britain's nuclear deterrent and voted in favour of replacing the UK's Trident nuclear weapons system while serving as an MP.
Since becoming foreign secretary, his comments on nuclear proliferation have focused primarily on Iran, repeatedly stressing that Tehran must not acquire a nuclear weapon.
It remains unclear whether Miliband will attend the UN nuclear disarmament meeting. His participation, or absence, could nevertheless draw attention to the tension between Britain's support for international nuclear non-proliferation and its continued maintenance of its own nuclear deterrent.

Ground broken for Makkoran’s history and culture museum in Chabahar
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-22
12:12:43 UTC
21:12:43 KST

Ground broken for Makkoran’s history and culture museum in Chabahar
TEHRAN - Ground was broken for the Makkoran’s history and culture museum in the Chabahar Free Zone on Tuesday, marking the start of a project aimed at documenting and showcasing the ancient history and cultural heritage of Iran’s Makkoran coast.
The ceremony was attended by Hossein Forouzan, secretary of Iran’s High Council of Free and Special Economic Zones; Mohammad-Saeid Arbabi, chief executive of the Chabahar Free Zone Organization; Alireza Noura, governor of Chabahar; and a number of provincial and regional officials.
Hamidreza Soleimani, CEO of the Dafineh Museums of the Mostazafan Foundation, said the museum was designed to provide a comprehensive and documented account of the ancient history and rich cultural heritage of the Makkoran coast.
The museum will be built on three floors, Soleimani said.
The ground floor will serve as the entrance and introductory area, where visitors will be introduced to the region through interactive touchscreens, sensory displays and other digital technologies.
The first floor will house archaeological artifacts and present the history of navigation and maritime trade in Makkoran, while the second floor will focus on the region’s development, infrastructure, industrial potential and contemporary transformations.
The museum will occupy a site of about 10,000 square meters, with a built-up area of approximately 2,500 square meters, according to Soleimani.
Under an earlier memorandum of understanding between the Chabahar Free Zone Organization and the Dafineh Museums Institute, the institute will oversee and provide specialist expertise for the museum’s design, content development and launch.
The Makkoran coast, also known as Makran or Mokran, is a largely semi-desert coastal strip along the Sea of Oman, extending across southeastern Iran and southwestern Pakistan. In Iran, the coast lies mainly in Sistan-Baluchestan province and includes Chabahar, a major port and commercial center on the Sea of Oman.

Taiwan removes low-value exemption for illegal e-cigarette imports
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-22
12:08:30 UTC
21:08:30 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The Ministry of Finance on Tuesday removed a low-value exemption from customs penalties for illegal imports of e-cigarettes and related products.
CNA reported that e-cigarettes, e-liquids, cartridges, and related components are no longer covered by an exemption from penalties for imported goods valued at NT$5,000 (US$158) or less. Customs authorities are also preparing guidelines that would increase fines for smuggling, false declarations, and other attempts to evade import restrictions.
Customs Administration Deputy Director-General Chao Tai-an (趙台安) said e-cigarette products have been used to consume new types of illegal drugs. He said authorities are strengthening border enforcement because of the risks to public safety.
Customs recorded 1,346 e-cigarette cases last year involving about 120,000 devices and 33,000 containers of e-liquid or cartridges. In the first eight months of this year, authorities recorded 726 cases involving about 35,000 devices and 40,000 containers of e-liquid or cartridges, per UDN.
Under the planned guidelines, violations such as smuggling or falsely declaring e-cigarette products would carry fines equal to 1.5 times the value of the goods. The higher penalties are intended to strengthen enforcement against prohibited vaping products entering Taiwan.
Travelers caught bringing prohibited e-cigarette products into Taiwan can have the goods confiscated. Cases may also be referred to local health authorities, with violations of tobacco control laws carrying fines starting at NT$50,000.
Customs said it will continue inspections to stop illegal e-cigarette products at the border. It also warned travelers not to bring them into Taiwan for personal use, as gifts, or on behalf of others.

Signs of a secret corridor and chambers discovered near Tutankhamun’s tomb

Signs of a secret corridor and chambers discovered near Tutankhamun’s tomb
Kyiv • UNN
Researchers recorded new underground anomalies near KV62, including a possible corridor two meters wide. The discovery supports the hypothesis of a Nefertiti complex.
Researchers have found new signs of unknown corridors and chambers near Tutankhamun’s tomb, KV62, in the Valley of the Kings. To do so, they conducted more than 1,200 measurements across an area of about 35 square meters, Daily Star reports, according to UNN.
Details
The most mysterious find was dubbed “anomaly 7.” The measurements indicate an area of reduced density containing an almost square object with higher density. Ballard suggests that it could be a chamber containing burial objects.
Of particular interest is a possible corridor about two meters wide branching off from Tutankhamun’s burial chamber. According to geophysicist George Ballard, it may be filled with debris, which could explain why previous studies failed to detect it.
The new results have once again revived the hypothesis of British Egyptologist Nicholas Reeves, who has suggested since 2015 that a larger complex associated with Nefertiti may be hidden behind Tutankhamun’s tomb.
Additionally
Pharaoh Tutankhamun ruled Egypt approximately from 1332 to 1323 BC. Ascending the throne at the age of about 8–9, he became one of the youngest rulers in history, which is why he is often called the “boy pharaoh.”
Queen Nefertiti ruled approximately from 1353 to 1336 BC as the principal (Great) Wife of Pharaoh Akhenaten (Amenhotep IV).
It will be recalled
In Egypt, archaeologists discovered the intact tomb of an official named Sekhentiu-Ptah, containing ritual objects.

Taiwan institute uses AI to sharpen drone thermal images
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-22
12:08:17 UTC
21:08:17 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The Institute for Information Industry said Tuesday that it had developed an AI system to improve the clarity of thermal images captured by drones, according to a press release.
Thermal imaging allows drones to operate at night and in other low-visibility conditions. However, high-end thermal sensors are expensive and vulnerable to supply-chain disruptions, making widespread deployment difficult.
The institute uses an AI super-resolution algorithm and edge computing to sharpen low-resolution thermal images captured with more affordable sensors. The algorithm reconstructs edges and contours to produce clearer images without requiring more expensive equipment.
Running the algorithm on an edge-computing chip allows images to be processed locally in real time. The resulting low latency makes the technology suitable for drone operations, the institute said.
The system is designed for nighttime patrols, search-and-rescue missions, and inspections in low-visibility environments. Clearer images can help operators locate heat sources more quickly.
The institute said it had also integrated domestically sourced chips, thermal cameras, and edge-computing modules to reduce dependence on foreign suppliers. It aims to offer the integrated system to businesses and other users.

Missouri airbase adds weapons storage building for incoming B-21s
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-22
12:08:09 UTC
21:08:09 KST

- The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers awarded K & K Industries $13.6 million to build a B-21 weapons release system storage facility at Whiteman Air Force Base, Missouri.
- The project is due for completion by March 31, 2028, part of roughly $900 million in planned B-21 construction work across Whiteman.
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers awarded K & K Industries a $13.6 million contract to build a weapons release system storage facility at Whiteman Air Force Base, Missouri, part of the base’s preparation to host the B-21 Raider stealth bomber. The Windsor, Missouri-based company’s firm-fixed-price award brings the project’s total value to $14,993,485.
Three companies bid on the project. Work will be done in Knob Noster, Missouri, the town adjacent to Whiteman, with an estimated completion date of March 31, 2028. The Army obligated $13,649,923 in fiscal 2026 military construction funds at the time of the award. The Kansas City District of the Army Corps of Engineers is managing the contract.
The facility will give Whiteman dedicated space to store and support armament-related equipment for the B-21, according to Air Force documentation on the project. It includes a new weapons and release-system shop covering about 1,580 square meters (17,000 square feet), along with alterations to roughly 674 square meters (7,250 square feet) of existing space, plus utilities, communications, access routes and site preparation work. Air Force documents describing the project say Whiteman currently lacks enough room to handle the munitions-related parts and equipment expected to arrive with the bomber.
Whiteman is home to the Air Force’s current B-2 Spirit fleet and is set to become the second operational base for the B-21, after Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota. The Air Force has said the new facility will let the base keep running B-2 operations without competing for existing infrastructure as B-21 support work ramps up.
This is one of roughly 30 military construction projects planned at Whiteman for the B-21 program, together valued at about $900 million, according to slides the Army Corps of Engineers presented at an industry day in September. Those projects include a dormitory and a radio-frequency hangar in addition to the weapons storage facility, with a weapons load trainer facility and a sustainment complex planned for awards in fiscal 2027.
The Army Corps separately awarded Conti Federal Services $74.8 million this month to build a radio-frequency and measurements hangar at Whiteman, a facility designed to check whether the B-21’s low-observable coatings and stealth characteristics hold up after maintenance or repairs. That hangar is scheduled for completion in September 2029.

Xi Jinping will demand an end to arms sales to Taiwan during his meeting with Trump - Reuters
Kyiv • UNN
China may demand an end to new and already ordered arms deliveries to Taiwan. Xi Jinping and Trump's talks will take place in Washington.
Chinese leader Xi Jinping may call on Washington to stop selling weapons to Taiwan during his upcoming meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump. Reuters was told this by sources familiar with the matter, reports UNN.
Details
It is noted that China will likely raise the issue of the third joint communiqué between the two countries, signed in 1982.
In the document, the United States stated its intention to gradually reduce arms sales to Taiwan and not pursue long-term arms deliveries to the island.
At the same time, then-U.S. President Ronald Reagan noted in an accompanying memorandum that Washington’s willingness to reduce arms sales depended on China’s continued commitment to a peaceful resolution of its differences with Taiwan.
China considers Taiwan its territory and regularly calls the island issue one of the most sensitive matters in relations with the United States. Beijing has repeatedly called on Washington to stop selling weapons to Taiwan.
China wants to stop deliveries that have already been ordered
According to the sources, China may call on the United States not only to halt new arms sales to Taiwan but also to stop supplying weapons that the island has already ordered.
One source said Xi Jinping may tell Trump that Taiwan itself is the source of instability in U.S.-China relations and is allegedly changing the status quo.
According to Reuters, China is instead offering to help the United States exert pressure on Iran in connection with the war in the Middle East.
The United States adheres to a “one China” policy, under which it does not officially determine Taiwan’s sovereignty but does not support Beijing’s position that the island is part of China.
In December, the Trump administration approved an $11 billion arms sales package for Taiwan — the largest in history. Another package worth approximately $14 billion has remained suspended for several months. After meeting with Xi Jinping in Beijing in May, Trump called this package “a very good bargaining chip.”
What they are saying in the United States
A White House representative said that Trump plans to make a decision on a new arms sales package for Taiwan fairly quickly.
During his first presidential term, Trump approved more arms sales to Taiwan than any other U.S. president. According to the White House representative, in the first year of his second term he has already approved more such sales than Joe Biden’s administration did over all four years.
Taiwan said it is closely monitoring high-level contacts between the United States and China and continues to maintain close communication with Washington.
Xi Jinping will arrive in Washington on Wednesday. Official talks with Trump are scheduled for Thursday, while the Chinese leader’s visit to the U.S. National Archives is scheduled for Friday.
At the same time, Senator Pete Ricketts Matt Pottinger said that he does not expect significant agreements on Taiwan during this week’s meetings.

Energy, defense sectors most attractive for investment in Ukraine despite war risks - survey
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-22
15:06:18 EEST
21:06:18 KST

The energy sector and defense industry top the list of the most promising areas for investment in Ukraine, according to Ukrainian and international business representatives.
That's according to a Business Ombudsman Council (BOC) survey, "Current Challenges to Business and Ukraine's Investment Attractiveness," in which 60% of respondents named energy as promising and 53.2% named the defense industry. The IT sector (42.5%), construction (38.1%) and agriculture (35.4%) also ranked among the top industries.
Despite the ongoing war, international interest in the Ukrainian market remains: none of the foreign business representatives surveyed said they had no interest at all in investing in Ukraine. More than a third of foreign companies (35%) rated their familiarity with the local business climate as high. Foreign investors consider direct investment in already-operating enterprises and forming joint business partnerships with Ukrainian companies to be the most common ways of entering the market.
War-related risks remain the main obstacle to opening or expanding foreign business, cited by 75% of respondents.
At the same time, institutional factors play a decisive role: to improve the investment climate, 90% of foreign investors point to the need to reduce corruption, 75% to simplifying administrative procedures, and 65% to ensuring access to justice. Tax incentives or the creation of special economic zones, by contrast, rank as much lower priorities for investors.
Ukraine's course toward EU integration has a strong positive effect on investment decisions for 94.9% of international companies, serving as a signal of long-term stability and regulatory alignment. Among Ukrainian businesses, meanwhile, 61.1% already actively export to EU countries, and another 9.9% plan to start exporting soon. Businesses cite high financial costs (45.5%), stiff competition (38.9%) and the difficulty of certifying products to European standards (36.2%) as the main barriers to entering the EU market.
The survey covered 319 Ukrainian companies from 20 regions. Fieldwork ran from May 14 to June 4, 2026.

Earlier, during a speech in parliament, Magyar, as quoted by DW, stated that Hungary is not a participant in the "Carpathian Eight" format initiated by Ukraine, "for good reasons," but did not explain them. He also opposed the construction of oil storage facilities in Hungary for Ukraine's needs, which Ukrainian "Naftogaz" and the Hungarian company MOL had agreed on.
"Prime Minister Magyar clearly stated that Hungary has not joined the C8 initiative, which is a fact. Moreover, no international energy cooperation can take place without the participation of the Hungarian government. Since the new Hungarian government came to power, it has made quite a few gestures toward Ukraine. Therefore, there is no analogy with the obstructionist policy pursued by Viktor Orban," Hungarian Foreign Minister Anita Orban added on X.

"Hannibal Holiday"
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-22
12:03:48 UTC

"Hannibal Holiday"
« previous post |
Today's Frazz:
Caulfield substitutes day for way, in the English translation of the Latin phrase "Aut inveniam viam aut faciam", which Wikipedia tells us "has been spuriously attributed to Carthaginian General Hannibal, in response to his generals statement that it was impossible to cross the Alps by elephant, during the Second Punic War in 218 BC". The fact that Caulfield frames the pun, and Frazz recognizes the reference, is a tribute to their shared erudition.
When I first learned this phrase many years ago, I wondered why the Romans would immortalize their enemy Hannibal. Perhaps it was like the British fascination with Napoleon? But apparently the only classical source for the phrase is Seneca's Hecules Furens, where it's used in the 3rd person singular to describe Hercules' return from the underworld. First-person versions appear as mottos in 16th-century England, and presumably the attribution to Hannibal started at some point after that.
I frequently walk past a first-person-plural version of the motto, over the Class of 1893 Memorial Gate on Spruce St. just west of 34th St.
In addition Penn's class of 1893, English-language Wikipedia lists several other British and American "social, educational and military organizations" who have adopted it as a motto. Italian Wikipedia gives a couple of Italian ones. And there's the fictional University of American Samoa.
